translations.text: The beginning of all wisdom is from God, and wisdom has been with him forever.
Who has counted the sand of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?
The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, the depth of the abyss, and wisdom—who has measured them?
Wisdom was created before all things.
And wisdom’s understanding dates from the creation of the world.
To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed?
And who has known her counsel?
There is one who is wise, and he is exceedingly awesome, and he sits upon his throne.
God himself created her, saw her, and measured her too.
He poured her out upon all his works, upon all flesh according to his generosity, and gave her to all who love her.
The fear of God is glory and a source of pride, gladness and a crown of joy.
The fear of God is gladness of heart. It gives joy, brings happiness, and prolongs the days of life.
For the one who fears God, his end will be good, and he will be blessed on the day of his death.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of God, and she was created with the faithful in their mothers’ wombs.
With human beings she was created as an everlasting foundation, and she remained faithful with their descendants.
The fullness of wisdom is the fear of God, and she satisfies them with her grain.
Her houses are full of gladness, and her fields are full of fruit.
The crown of wisdom is the fear of God. It brings peace, healing, and life.
Her Creator saw her and measured her. He made a spring of knowledge, counsel, and wisdom flow, and he made those who hold fast to her great and honored them.
The root of wisdom is the fear of God, and her branches prolong the days of life.
An angry and unjust person cannot be justified, for when he rages, it brings about his downfall.
Endure anger patiently until its time passes, and afterward it will make you glad.
Keep your words hidden until you find the right time, and many will speak of your wisdom.
In wisdom’s treasuries is the teaching of proverbs. A sinner provokes one who fears God.
If you love wisdom, keep her commandments, and God will give her to you.
Wisdom and knowledge are the fear of God, and his will is faith and gentleness.
Do not forget the fear of the Lord.
Do not attach yourself to him with a divided heart, doubting.
Do not become a target of people's talk, and guard your lips.

Do not exalt yourself, so that you are not disgraced and your soul does not fall. The Lord will expose your secrets and bring you down in the midst of many, because you did not come in the fear of the Lord, and your heart is full of deceit.
My son, if you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for suffering.
Set your heart right and be patient. Do not waver, and when you are in distress, do not doubt.
But follow the Lord and do not abandon him, so that your life may be prolonged in your later years.
Accept everything that happens to you, and be patient in the days of your humiliation.
For gold is tested in fire, and a righteous person is tested through the suffering of humiliation.
But trust in the Lord, and he will help you. Make your paths straight and rely on him.
You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy, and do not turn away from him, so that you do not fall.
You who fear the Lord, trust in him, and do not lose your reward.
You who fear the Lord, hope for his goodness and for the joy of his everlasting mercy.
Look back to ancient times and consider: Who trusted in the Lord and was put to shame? Who persevered in the fear of him and was abandoned by him? Who called on him and was ignored?
For the Lord is merciful and compassionate. He forgives sins and saves in the day of distress.
Woe to the doubting heart, to slack hands, and to the sinner who follows two paths and walks crookedly!
Woe to the doubting heart, because it has not trusted; therefore it will not be delivered.
Woe to those who have lost their reward! What will they do when the Lord turns to them?
Those who fear the Lord will not forget his word, and those who love him will keep his commandment and his ways.
Those who fear the Lord will seek his will, and those who love him will be filled with his law.
Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts and afflict themselves before him.
Let us fall into the hands of the Lord rather than into human hands, for his mercy is as great as his majesty.
Listen to me, your father, my children, and do this so that you may live.
For the Lord has honored the father above his children and exalted the mother's authority over her children.
Whoever honors his father will have his sins forgiven.
Whoever honors his mother is like someone storing up treasure.
Whoever honors his father will rejoice in his children, and his Creator will hear him when he prays.
Whoever honors his father will have a long life.
Whoever obeys the Lord will give his mother rest.
He will serve the one who fathered him as his servants do.
Honor your father in both your words and your deeds, so that his blessing may reach you.
A father’s blessing strengthens the houses of his children, but a mother’s curse tears up their foundations.
Do not boast about your father's dishonor, for your father's dishonor brings you no glory. A person is honored through his father's honor, and a mother's dishonor brings disgrace to her child.
My son, bear with your father’s forgetfulness, and do not grieve him during his lifetime.

Even if he grows old and his mind fails, agree with him and honor him as much as you can. Do not mistreat your father because of his forgetfulness, for the reward for your kindness to your father will not be forgotten.
In place of sin, righteousness will be built up for you.
It will be remembered in your favor on the day of your distress. As the sun melts frost, so it will melt away your sins.
Whoever abandons his father is disgraced, and whoever angers his mother is cursed before God.
My son, let your deeds be seen in your faith, and righteous people will love you.
The greater you become, the more you should humble yourself, and you will find a reward with God.
For the Lord's work is great, and he is praised among the humble and the holy.
Do not seek what is too difficult for you, or inquire into what is beyond your ability. Instead, reflect on what you have been commanded.
Do not let what is hidden lead you astray.
Do not investigate the multitude of your affairs, for you have been shown things beyond human understanding.
Their presumption has led many astray, and the pride of their hearts has brought many down.
Whoever loves danger will die in it. An evil heart will suffer in the end.
An evil heart will be scourged with suffering, and a sinner will add sin to his sins.
There is no cure for the affliction of the proud, for an evil plant has taken root in them.
A wise heart considers proverbs, and an understanding ear loves wisdom.
Water puts out a blazing fire, and almsgiving brings forgiveness of sin.
For someone who repays a kindness, it will be remembered later, and on the day he slips he will find support.
My son, do not deprive a poor person of his livelihood, and do not turn your eyes away from someone who asks you for help.
Do not cause a hungry person pain, and do not anger someone who is sorrowful.
Do not distress a troubled heart, and do not pass by someone who asks you for help.
Do not be angry with the servant who serves you, and do not turn your face away from the poor.
Do not turn your eyes away from someone who asks you for help, and do not give him a reason to curse you.
For if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, his Creator will hear his prayer.
Make yourself loved among the people, serve rulers, and do not exalt yourself.
Listen to the poor person, and answer him kindly with gentle words.
Rescue the oppressed from the hand of his oppressor, and do not be reluctant to judge his case.
Be like a father to an orphan, and stand in the place of a husband to his mother. Then you will be like a son of the Most High, and he will love you more than your mother does.
Wisdom exalts her children and welcomes those who seek her.
Whoever loves her loves his own life, and whoever comes to her will be filled with joy.
Whoever holds fast to her will inherit honor, and wherever she enters, the Lord will bless.
Those who serve her serve the Holy One, and the Lord loves those who love her.
Whoever listens to her will judge nations, and whoever pays attention to her will live securely.
If you trust her, you will find her, and she will make you great during your lifetime.
At first she will walk with him, frightening him, terrifying him, alarming him, punishing him, and teaching him until she has trained his soul. She will test him with discipline.
After this she will receive him again, make him glad, and reveal her counsel to him.
But if he strays from her, she will abandon him and hand him over to what will bring about his downfall.
Watch for the right time, beware of evil, and do not let shame make you show partiality at your own expense.
For there is a shame through which a person commits sin, and there is a shame through which a person acts rightly and finds favor.
Do not show favoritism when it will harm your own soul, and do not let shame cause your downfall.
Do not prevent a speaker from speaking, for his wisdom is known from his words, and his learning from what he says.
Do not deny the truth, and accept rebuke for your mistakes.
Do not be ashamed to confess your errors, and do not try to overpower the current of a river.
Do not humble yourself before a foolish man, and do not show partiality to a powerful person.
Fight for what is right until death, for the Lord your God will fight for you.
Do not be rash with your mouth, and do not neglect your work.
Do not act like a lion in your house, and do not terrorize the servant who serves you faithfully.
Do not stretch out your hands to borrow, then draw back and hide your right hand when it is time to repay.
Do not squander your possessions for nothing, and do not say, “My wealth is enough for me.”
Do not follow the unchecked power of your own will.
Do not say, “I am powerful, and who can overcome me?” For the Lord will surely take vengeance.
Do not say, “I have sinned, and I have suffered no punishment,” for the Lord is very patient.
Do not be afraid to turn back because of your sins, and do not add sin to your sin, saying, “The Lord’s mercy is great.”
Both mercy and punishment come from him; his punishment descends upon the sinner.
Do not delay turning back to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day, for destruction comes suddenly, and you will grieve when your punishment and scourging come.
Do not covet unjust wealth, for it cannot save you in your time of distress.
Do not winnow in every wind, and do not pursue everything you desire. Do not be like a sinner who has two tongues.
But stand firm in your wisdom, and let your word be consistent.
Be quick to listen and patient in giving an answer.
If you know something, tell your neighbor; otherwise, put your hand over your mouth.
Both your disgrace and your honor come from your speech, and a person’s downfall comes from his tongue.
Do not be a slanderer, and do not revile others with your tongue. A thief's shame is small, but the disgrace of someone with a double tongue is great.
Show yourself kind to both the great and the small.
Be a friend rather than an enemy, for a bad name brings disgrace and reproach. So it is also with a sinner who has two tongues.
Do not exalt yourself by following your own counsel, lest your soul be torn apart like an ox.
It will eat your leaves, destroy your fruit, and leave you like a withered tree.
An unruly soul destroys the person who possesses it and makes him [?] before his enemies.
A pleasant tongue increases friendship, and a pleasant mouth increases the number of friends.
Let many be your friends, but let the one with whom you discuss your plans be one in ten thousand.
When you make a friend, make him your friend in the days of your distress, and do not trust him too much.
For there is a friend who is passing and lasts only a few days; he will not stand by you on the day of your distress.
There is a friend who becomes your enemy, slanders you, and exposes your secrets.
There is a friend who befriends you because of your table, but he will not be there for you; when you are in distress, he leaves you.
When you prosper, he will be like you and will give orders to your household.
But when you are in distress, he will become your enemy and hide from you so that you cannot see him.
Keep away from your enemies, and be on your guard with your friends.
A faithful friend is like a strong shield, and whoever finds one has found a treasure.
There is no substitute for a faithful friend, and nothing compares with his speech.
A faithful friend is a remedy for life, and those who fear the Lord will find one.
Whoever fears the Lord will make his friendship upright, for his companion will be like him.
My son, choose wisdom from your youth, and you will find her even into your old age.
Go to her like someone who plows and sows, and wait for her blessed fruit. For you will toil only a little in cultivating her, and soon you will eat grain.
She is very troublesome to fools, and she will not remain with someone who lacks understanding.
Like a testing stone when someone lifts it, she weighs heavily on him, and he soon throws her away.
Wisdom is what her name says she is, and not many know her.
Listen to me, my son, and patiently accept my counsel. Do not disregard my correction.
Put your feet into her fetters, and place her collar around your neck.
Lower your shoulders and carry her, and do not resent her chains.
Go to her with all your soul, and keep her ways with all your strength.
Follow her footsteps and seek her, and you will find her. Take hold of her and do not let her go.
In the end you will find rest, and she will become a joy to you.
Her chains will become a strong shield for you, and her collar will become a robe of honor for you.
For everlasting gold is with her, and her bonds will become an ornament of jacinth for you.
You will wear her like a robe of honor, and she will crown you with a crown of joy.
If you wish, my son, you will become wise; and if you apply yourself, you will learn.
If you love to listen, be patient; and if you incline your ear, you will hear wisdom.
Stand among a gathering of elders, and follow anyone among them whom you see to be wise.
Be quick to listen to every word of Scripture, and do not forget a wise saying.
If you see a wise man, go to him, and let his heel wear down the threshold of his door.
Reflect on the Lord’s commandments and read his Scriptures at all times. He will strengthen your heart and grant you the love of wisdom.
Do not do evil, and evil will not overtake you.
Keep away from wrongdoing, and it too will keep away from you.
Do not sow in the furrow of sin, so that you do not reap it sevenfold.
Do not ask the Lord for kingship, or ask a king for a seat of honor.
Do not claim to be righteous before the Lord, or pretend to be wise before a king.
Do not desire to become a judge, lest you be unable to punish the offender, or show partiality to a powerful person and bring sin into the midst of justice.
Do not sin against the people of your town, and do not lead yourself astray among your people.
Do not bind two sins together or combine them, for you will not escape punishment even for a single deed.
Do not say, “Because of my many offerings, the Lord will forgive me, and because I have brought offerings to the Most High Lord, he will have mercy on me.”
Do not be fainthearted when you pray, and do not neglect giving alms.
Do not laugh at a person who is grieving, for there is one who brings sorrow and who brings joy.
Do not cultivate a lie against your neighbor, and do not do this against your friend or companion.
Do not love falsehood at any time or in any matter, for in the end it will harm you.
Do not babble among the elders. Do not retract the vow you have spoken with your mouth, and do not change your word.
Do not neglect the work of your hands or the crops your Creator causes to grow for you.
Do not join with sinners, even if they are numerous.
Remember that [?] will not delay. Humble yourself all the more, for the punishment of sinners is worms and fire.
Do not exchange a friend for a meal, and do not lose your friend for red gold.
Do not hate a wise and good wife, for her favor is worth more than gold.
Do not treat harshly your servant who serves you faithfully, or your hired worker who devotes his life to you.
Love your wise servant more than yourself. Do not withhold his wages, and set him free as he has hoped you would.
Never neglect to care for your livestock, and keep near you those among them that are useful to you.
If you have children, discipline them and teach them; bow their necks from their youth.
If you have daughters, guard them and do not lead them astray. Do not laugh with them or indulge them.
Bring your daughter to maturity and guard her. You will have accomplished a great task and found relief. Give her in marriage to a wise man.
If you have a wife who is like your own soul, do not send her away.
Honor your father with all your heart, and do not forget your mother’s suffering.
Remember that you were born through them. What will you give them in return for what they have done for you?
Fear the Lord with all your soul, and honor his priests.
Love your Creator with all your strength, and do not abandon those who serve him.

Fear the Lord and honor the one who serves him. Give him the share commanded to you: the firstfruits, the sin offering, the shoulder portions, the sacred sacrifices, and the first portions of the holy things.
Stretch out your hand to the poor, so that your blessing may be complete.
You will receive the reward of your generosity for your whole soul. Do not withhold your kindness even from the dead.
Do not withdraw from those who weep, and mourn with those who mourn.
Do not be reluctant to visit the sick, and for this they will love you.
In everything you say, remember your end, and you will never sin.
Do not quarrel with powerful men, lest you fall into their hands.
Do not contend with someone richer than you, lest he overpower you with his wealth. For many have been destroyed because of red gold, and it has corrupted the hearts of kings.
Do not argue with a talkative man; otherwise you will be throwing wood onto a fire.
Do not laugh and jest with a fool, lest you disgrace your relatives.
Do not reproach someone who is repenting for his wrongdoing. Remember that we are all sinners.
Do not mistreat anyone because of his forgetfulness, for among us too there are those who forget.
Do not rejoice over someone who has died. Remember that we will all die.
Do not disregard the words of the wise, and learn their proverbs, for through them you will find wisdom and serve rulers.
Heed the instruction of the elders, for they too learned from their fathers. You too will learn from them, find what to say in times of distress, and know how to answer.
Do not stir up the fire of sinners, lest you be burned by their flame.
Do not exchange words with a hostile slanderer, lest he lead you astray with the words of his mouth.
Do not lend to someone richer than you. If you do lend to him, consider it lost.
Do not guarantee a debt for someone stronger than you. If you do guarantee it, expect to pay it yourself.
Do not go to court against a ruler, for they will decide the case in his favor because of his rank.
Do not travel together with a reckless man, lest he turn violently against you. For he does whatever his heart desires, and you will die because of his folly.
Do not quarrel with a hot-tempered man or go out into the countryside with him. For shedding blood is nothing in his eyes, and he will take you where there is no help.
Do not consult a fool, for he cannot keep secret what he has heard.
Do not tell a stranger about your distress, for you do not know what may come upon you.
Do not reveal what is in your heart to everyone, lest ruin become your reward.
Do not be jealous over the wife of your bosom, lest she learn an evil lesson to use against you.
Do not give yourself over to a woman, lest she trample on your strength.
Do not go astray with another man's wife, lest you fall into her snares.
Do not dance with a female musician, lest she ensnare you with her singing.
Do not strip a virgin naked, lest desire for her lead you astray.
Do not give yourself over to a prostitute, lest you lose your inheritance.
Do not roam the streets of the city, lest its blossoms lead you astray.
Turn your eyes away from a beautiful woman, and do not let another man's wife's beauty attract you. Many have gone astray because of a woman's beauty, and because of this love burns like fire.
Do not sit with another man's wife or revel with her over drinks, lest your soul become bound to her and your spirit slip into death.
Do not abandon your old friend, for a newly acquired friend will not be like him to you. A new friend is new wine; when it has aged, you will drink it with joy.
Do not envy the wealth of sinners, for you do not know how they will be destroyed.
Do not be attracted by the pleasures of the wicked. Remember that they will not be justified before they die.

Keep far away from rulers who condemn people to death, and no fear of death will come upon you. But if you approach them, make no mistake, so that you do not lose your life. Know that you are passing among snares and walking among pitfalls.
Do good to your neighbor as much as you can, and seek advice from the wise.
Let your deliberations be with wise people, and let all your conversation concern the law of God.
Let righteous men be at your meal, and let your meal be in the fear of God.
A craftsman’s work shines in his hands, and a ruler of nations is praised for the wisdom of his speech.
A talkative man is feared in his city, and people continually hate him because of his speech.
A wise king disciplines his subjects, and an understanding ruler establishes order.
As the ruler of a people is, so are his servants; and as the governor of a city is, so do those within it act.
A foolish king destroys his people, but a city stands firm through the wisdom of its learned leaders.
The government of the earth is in God's hands.
A scribe’s wisdom is known from his face.
Do not insult your neighbor for any wrong he has done, and do not do anything evil by insulting him.
Pride is hateful to God and to humanity, and injustice is worse than anything.
Sovereignty passes from one people to another because of injustice, oppression, and wealth.
Why, then, are earth and dust proud, when a person rots even while still alive?
A physician can heal even a serious wound, but someone who is king today will die tomorrow.
Once a person has died, he becomes a portion for worms.
Pride begins by leading a person away from God and making his heart deny his Creator.
The beginning of pride is sin, and it heaps impurity upon anyone who clings to it. Because of this, God reveals their punishment and destroys them forever.
God overthrew the thrones of rulers and appointed the meek in their place.
God uprooted the nations and planted the humble in their place.
God erased the traces of the nations and destroyed them down to the foundations of the earth.
He uprooted them and destroyed them, and erased their memory from the earth.
Pride was not created for humanity, nor wrath and raging anger for those born of women.

Among human offspring, which offspring is honorable? The offspring of those who fear God. Among human offspring, which offspring is dishonorable? The offspring of those who do not keep the commandment.
A ruler is honored above his neighbor, but those who fear God are honored above him.
For the rich, the honored, and the poor alike, their reason for boasting is the fear of God.
It is not right to mistreat a poor person because of his poverty, nor is it right to honor a sinful man because of his wealth.
Elders, rulers, and judges are honored, but none of them is greater than someone who fears God.
A wise servant serves blamelessly, and a knowledgeable man is no better than he.
Do not try to be clever when doing your work, and do not exalt yourself in times of hardship.
Someone who serves and works is better than someone who struts about and boasts but cannot find food.
My son, honor yourself with humility, and provide for yourself as well as you can.
Someone who wrongs himself—to whom will he be good? And who will praise someone who does not provide for himself?
People praise a poor man for his wisdom, and commend a rich man for his wealth.
Someone who does not grieve when he is poor—how will he rejoice when he prospers?
A poor man is honored for his wisdom and sits among rulers.
Do not favor someone because of his beauty, and do not despise someone because of his wretchedness.
The bee is smaller than all flying creatures, but its produce is sweeter than anything else.
Do not boast about the beauty of your clothing, and do not exalt yourself in your days of honor, for God's work is wonderful, and his skill is hidden from human beings.
Many rulers have fallen to the ground, while a solitary man has been crowned.
Many great men have been deeply humiliated, and many honored men have come under another's power.
Do not condemn someone without questioning him. Investigate first, and then rebuke.
Do not answer before you have heard, and do not interrupt another person's speech.
Do not involve yourself in a matter that is not your concern, and do not contend with a sinner's bow.
My son, do not multiply your activities, for if you multiply them, you will not have room to act rightly. If you run, you will not escape, and if you pursue righteousness, you will not attain it.
For there is someone who hurries, works, and toils, yet becomes poorer still.

And there is someone who, though weak, does not ask, who [?] and can do nothing. Even if he makes an effort, he becomes poorer still. But when God looks on him favorably, he lifts him out of his poverty.
He makes him great and honors him, and many people marvel at him.
Both good and evil,
both life and death,
both poverty and wealth come from God.
God's grace visits the righteous, and his favor makes the world glad.
There is someone who becomes rich through much toil and careful saving, and this is how he gains his enjoyment.

When he hopes to rest and says, “I will eat and drink; now I will take my ease, for I have stored up provisions,” he does not know the day that will overtake him, when he will leave everything to someone else and die.
Stand firm in the fear of God, learn through it, and grow old at your work.
Do not let the deeds of sinners entice you. Trust in God and hope for the reward of your labor, for everything is easy for God: all at once, in an instant, he makes a poor man rich.
The blessing of God is the reward of the righteous, and his blessing upon the righteous person increases.
Do not say, “There is no need, then,” and do not say, “There is no reward for me, then.”
“From now on I have enough, and from now on [?].”
On a good day, people forget the bad, and on a bad day, they forget the good.
For on the day of death it is easy for God, for he repays each person according to his conduct.
On an evil day, prosperity is forgotten, and at a person's end his deeds become known.
Do not call a person blessed before you see his end, for a person’s way of life is revealed through his children.
Do not bring everyone you meet into your house, for a treacherous person has many ways of outwitting you.
A partridge is trapped among the leaves of [?]; so is the heart of an arrogant man. Like a spy, he watches for another’s downfall.
A treacherous person repays you with evil in return for good and disgraces you for faults you do not have.
As the sparks of a fire increase, its coals increase, and a sinful man endangers his own life.
Guard yourself against an evil person, for he creates evil, so that he does not bring lasting disgrace upon you.
If you lodge a stranger with you, he will disturb you, lead you astray, and deprive you of your possessions.
When you do good, know whom you are doing it for, so that you may receive a reward for your goodness.
Do good to a righteous person, and you will receive your reward. If you do not receive it from him, you will receive it from his Creator.
There is no good for someone who does evil or for someone who does not give alms.
Give to a righteous person, so that a sinner does not take from you.

Do good to the poor, and do not give to an evil person. Withhold your food so that he does not take it from you and attack you with your own possessions. For you will receive twice as much evil from him in repayment for all the good you have done for him.
For God hates sinners and takes vengeance on the wicked.
Give to a righteous person rather than to a sinner.
Your friend will not reveal himself to you in your happiness, and your enemy will not hide himself from you in your distress.
Your happiness wounds your enemies, and your adversity drives your friends away.
Never trust your enemy, for the evil in his heart is like rust on iron.
Even if you [?], he will set a trap for you without praising you. Strengthen yourself and guard against him. Be to him like a remover of rust, and he will never overcome you.

Do not place him beside you, lest he injure you and take your place. Do not seat him at your right hand, lest he take your position of authority. In the end you will come to understand my words and remember my warning.
Who will plead for a serpent of the earth or for any evil beast?
So it is with someone who walks with a sinful man and joins in his sin.
Your enemy will stand beside you for a time; when you turn around, you will no longer see him, and he will not stay with you.

Your enemy makes his words sweet to you with his lips, but in his heart he plots to throw you into a pit. Your enemy even sheds tears for you, but once he has led you astray, he will not have enough of your blood.
If you fall into distress, you will find him before your face ahead of everyone else; and before the one who helps you, he lowers his head beneath your feet.
He will clap his hands and shake his head, and then turn his face away and mock you.
Anyone who touches pitch will be stained by it, and anyone who befriends an arrogant person will become like him.

Do not lift a heavy weight or carry it on your shoulders, and do not join your possessions with those of someone stronger and richer than you. How can a metal pot be friends with an earthenware pot? For it is the earthenware pot that is damaged, makes a noise, and breaks.
Likewise, the rich man does wrong and then becomes indignant, while the poor man suffers wrong and then laments.
If you have something useful to him, he will draw you close to himself; but if you are drained, he will no longer look at you.
If you have possessions, he will associate with you and use up what belongs to you, and afterward he will no longer recognize you.
If he has a concern that troubles him, he will treat you kindly, fill you with great hopes, smile at you, speak kindly to you, and say to you, “What do you want?”

With his food he will entice you once, and a second and third time he will strip you bare. After this he will turn away and will not listen to you. Even if he sees you, he will laugh at you and shake his head at you.
Take care that he does not mislead you or make a fool of you, and do not bring sorrow into your joy.
Whatever a great man tells you, say “Yes” to him. If he invites you, do not refuse him, and he will love you all the more.
Do not keep far away or disappear, and do not remain distant for long, so that he does not forget you.
Do not talk too much with him, and do not trust his many words, for through his many words he will test you, and he will question you as though he were joking with you.
The person who draws out his companion’s plans has no mercy, for he is not troubled by his companion’s being bound and [?].
Be alert and guard yourself against him, for you are walking with your killer.
Every animal loves its own kind, and every person loves his fellow.
Every living creature gathers with its own kind, and people follow those of their own kind.
How can a wolf be friends with a lamb? It is the same with a sinner and a righteous person.
Who can reconcile dogs with wolves, and who can make a poor person friends with a rich person?
Likewise, the rich man detests the poor man.
The arrogant person despises the person who humbles himself; likewise, the rich man despises the poor man.
If a rich man totters, his friends support him; but if a poor man falls, his companions drive him away.

If a rich man slips, many people lift him up, and if he speaks, they put his words right for him. But if a poor man makes a mistake, they curse him, and even if he speaks well, they do not listen to him.

When a rich man speaks, everyone falls silent. They praise his words and exalt him to the clouds. But if a poor man speaks well, they say to him, “Who is this?” And if he stumbles, they knock him down.
Wealth is good when you do not commit sin, but a sinner condemns his poverty with his own mouth.
A person’s heart changes his face, whether he is joyful or sorrowful.
A bright face is the sign of a joyful heart, and you will find wise counsel through your labor.
Happy is the person who does not stumble in his speech; but sorrow does not alarm the sinner.
Happy is the person who does not distress himself and has not lost his hope.
Wealth is not fitting for a man who does not understand a word, and possessions are not fitting for a miser.
One who deprives himself stores up wealth for someone else, and another will revel in his possessions.
To whom will someone who begrudges himself be generous, someone who does not enjoy his own possessions?
There is no one worse than someone who begrudges himself, and this is the punishment for his wickedness.
Even if he does good, he does it only when he forgets; afterward he reveals his wickedness.
The miser has an evil eye; he turns his face away and blinds himself.
A greedy eye is not satisfied with its share, and the wickedness of his heart wears away his bones.
The eye of a sick man begrudges food, and they are dismayed at the table.
My son, provide for yourself as well as you can, and bring an offering to God according to your means.
Remember that death will not delay, and you have not reckoned the day of death.
Before you die, do good to your neighbor, and open your hand and give as much as you can.
Do not deprive yourself of your day of enjoyment, and do not let a share of good things escape you.
Will you not leave the fruit of your toil to someone else, and will your heirs not divide everything you have worked for?
Receive and give, and bring yourself joy, for you will find no enjoyment in the grave.
Every living being wears out like clothing, for the command of the law was established: "You will surely die."
As with the leaves of a tree whose foliage is thick—the earlier leaves fall and later ones sprout—so it is with every generation of flesh and blood: one is born and another dies.
Every work wears out, and he perishes with it.
But blessed is the man who died while wise, who learned and preserved his wisdom.
And who considers wisdom’s ways in his heart and learns her secrets.
Follow after her, seek her tracks, and watch her paths.
He peers through her windows and listens at her doors.
He lodges near her house and plants his stakes in her walls.
He sets up his tent within her hands and [?] in her fine dwelling.
He settles his children in her shade and spends the night beneath her branches.
He shelters beneath her from the heat and rests within her glory.
One who fears the Lord will do this, and one who keeps his law will find her.
She will meet him like his mother and embrace him like a virgin wife.
She will feed him the bread of wisdom and give him the water of understanding to drink.
He will lean on her and will not be shaken; he will trust in her and will not be put to shame.
She will exalt him above his companion and open his mouth in the midst of the multitude.
She will give him a crown of (wisdom and) joy and gladness, and he will inherit an everlasting name.
But fools will not find her, and sinners will not see her.
She is far from the proud, and liars do not remember her.
The words of a sinner’s mouth are not fitting, for he does not speak in the fear of God.
They tell parables with wisdom, and God helps the one who learns.
Do not say, “It was because of the Lord that I fell away,” and do not do what he hates.
And do not say, “He led me astray,” for he does not desire a sinful person.
For God hates everything unclean. [?]
He created human beings in the beginning and left them free to do as they wished.
If you wish, you can keep his commandments and faithfully carry out his will.
Look, he has placed fire and water before you, so that you may stretch out your hand toward whichever you choose.
Life and death are before a human being, and whichever he chooses will be given to him.
For the Lord’s wisdom is great, his power is mighty, and he knows and sees everything.
His eyes are on those who fear him, and he knows every deed of human beings.
He has commanded no one to commit sin, nor has he given permission, nor have they asked him to let them sin.
Do not desire many children who are worthless, and do not rejoice in wicked children.
Even if they become numerous, do not rejoice in them if the fear of God is not upon them.
Do not count on their survival, and do not let their numbers make you glad. One is better than a thousand, and dying childless is better than having a wicked child.
For through one wise person a city becomes strong, but a multitude of sinners will perish.
My eyes have seen many such things, and my ears have heard things greater than these.
Fire burns in the assembly of sinners, and wrath blazes against a rebellious people.
The people of old who grew great did not save themselves, though they trusted in their strength.
He did not spare the region where Lot lived, whose people exalted themselves and made life bitter for Lot.
And he did not spare the sinful people who banded together in their sins:
They were six hundred thousand men on foot who gathered together and made their hearts evil.
Even if there is only one person who stiffens his neck, it would be astonishing if he escaped. For both mercy and punishment come from him, and he is able both to show mercy and to bring punishment.
As great as his mercy is, so also is his correction, and he repays people according to their deeds.
A sinner will not escape [?], and a righteous person will not lose the reward for his endurance.
Every act of charity brings mercy, and everyone receives according to his conduct.
Do not say, “I will escape from the Lord, and there is no one in heaven who will find me. Among the many nations there is no one who knows me. And what does my life count for in the whole world?”
Look, heaven, the heaven above heaven, the abyss, and the earth—all these tremble when he visits them.
The mountains and the foundations of the earth shake and tremble when he looks at them.
Yet the heart does not consider this. Who can understand his ways?
No human being can see his storm, and the greater part of his work is hidden.
Who can teach his righteous works, and who can await the outpouring of his mercy?
A person lacking understanding thinks this way; a foolish and misguided person thinks foolishly.
Listen to me, my child, and learn wisdom. Listen attentively to my words with your heart.
Display your wisdom as is fitting for you, in due order, and examine the message of your instruction.
The Lord's works were created by his judgment, and he distinguished their appointed arrangements, each in its course.
He arranged all his works so that the world would endure, and their hosts according to their created natures. They neither thirst nor hunger, and their work never ceases.
One does not collide with another, and they will never disobey his word.
After this, the Lord looked upon the earth and filled it with all his blessing.
He filled the earth with the spirit of every living thing, and into the earth they return.
God created human beings from the earth, and he will return them to it again.
He gave them a numbered span of years and days and made them rulers over everything in it.
He clothed them each with their own strength and made them in his own likeness.
He made every living creature fear them and gave them dominion over wild animals and birds.
He gave them speech, a tongue, eyes, ears, and a heart with which to think.
He filled them with the knowledge of wisdom and showed them both evil and good.
He placed fear in their hearts to show them the greatness of his work,
so that they might speak of the greatness of his work,
so that they might praise his holy name.
He gave them wisdom and granted them as an inheritance the law that gives them life.
He made an everlasting covenant with them and told them his judgments.
Their ears [?] heard the voice of his glory.
He commanded them all concerning their neighbors.
Their ways are before him at all times, and they have nowhere to hide from his eyes.
He appointed kings over all the nations, but Israel became the Lord’s portion.
All their deeds are before him like the sun, and his eyes continually watch their ways.
Their sins are not hidden from him, and all their wrongdoings are before God.
A person’s almsgiving is like a seal kept with him; a person’s reward is guarded for him like the pupil of an eye.
Afterward he will return and repay them, and he will bring the punishment for their sins upon their heads.
Yet he gave them a way to repent, and he brings joy to those who have abandoned hope.
Return to the Lord and abandon sin; plead before him and repent of your wrongdoing.
Return to the Most High, turn away from injustice, and hate everything unclean all the more.
Who will praise the Most High in the grave, as the living do who give him thanks?
For someone who has died and become as nothing, repentance has passed him by. While you are alive, praise the Lord with joy.
For God's mercy is great, and he shows mercy to those who praise him.
For a human being cannot be everything, because a human being is mortal.
What is brighter than the sun? Yet even it grows dark, and flesh and blood devises evil.
He does not know the power of the heights of heaven, and every human being is dust and earth.
He who lives forever created everything together.
The Lord alone is righteous.
No one can [?] know his work, and who knows the extent of his greatness?
Who has counted the might of his power, and who can describe his mercy precisely?
There is nothing to add and nothing to take away, and no one can discover the extent of the Lord’s glory.
When he creates a human being, he commands him at that time; and when he gives him authority, he gives him rest at that time.
What is a human being, and what use is he? What is his goodness, and what is his wickedness?
The number of his days is a hundred years.
Like a single drop of water among all the waters of the sea, and like a single grain of sand among all the sand, so are his few years among all the days of eternity.
For this reason the Lord is patient with them and pours out his mercy upon them.
He saw them and knew that their end was evil; therefore he increased his mercy.
A person has mercy on his neighbor, but the Lord alone has compassion on every living being. He disciplines, teaches, and brings them back, as a shepherd does his flock.
He has compassion on those who patiently endure his discipline and on those who follow his law.
My child, do not bring sorrow into joy, and do not speak harshly when giving anything.
Does not rain cool the heat? In the same way, a kind word is better than a gift.
Look, then: a kind word comes before a gift, and both are found with a righteous person.
And a hard-hearted person gives without his heart being moved, while a fool insults and gives no thanks.
Before you speak, inquire; and before you become ill, seek healing.
Before you are judged, examine yourself, and you will find mercy in the time of your distress.
Before you grow weak, humble yourself, and repent when you sin.
Do not delay fulfilling your vow, and carry it out righteously before you die.
Before you make a vow, prepare yourself for it, and do not be like someone who puts God to the test.
When you become angry, remember the day of death; remember the day of your punishment, turn back, and repent.
Remember days of hunger during days of plenty, and remember days of hardship during days of prosperity.
For circumstances change from morning to evening, and everything happens swiftly with God. (Concerning honey.)
A wise man is cautious in everything and keeps watch over himself. And in the days when you sin, repent.
Every discerning person finds wisdom, and she makes the person who finds her faithful and reverent.
Those who understand words become wise in their own hearts and speak carefully considered proverbs.
Do not go after or follow the desire for sin, and restrain yourself from evil desire.
If you give your soul what it desires, it will make you a source of boldness for your enemy.
Do not borrow when you are poor, lest you become trapped when you have nothing at all in your purse.
A trader and a drunkard will not become rich; whoever neglects a little will lose much.
Drink and women lead a wise man astray, and whoever follows a prostitute is in the wrong.
And his end is worms and decay; a disgraced soul will not return.
Whoever is quick to believe is shallow-hearted, and whoever commits sin does wrong against his own soul.
Whoever indulges his heart will become estranged, and whoever hates excessive talk will lessen his sin.
Do not disclose a word you have heard or repeat it, and it will never harm you.
Say nothing to either friend or enemy, and do not disclose your offense—what you have heard [?].
For if he has heard it, he will not keep it hidden for you, but will lie in wait for you.
Until you die, do not disclose a matter you have heard; then be confident that no harm will come upon you.
A fool is restless until he tells the news he has heard, and he writhes like a woman in labor giving birth to a child.
Just as someone who has been wounded groans as he pulls an arrow out of himself, so a fool groans to let out a word he has heard.
Reprove your friend; perhaps he did not do it. And even if he did, reprove him so that he will not do it again.
Reprove your friend; perhaps he did not say it. And even if he did, reprove him so that he will not repeat it.
Rebuke your friend; perhaps they have accused him out of hatred. Do not believe every word they have told you.
For there is someone who goes wrong without intending it in his heart. And who is there who does not go wrong with his tongue?
Correct your friend before anger grows. Let wicked anger pass away for the sake of God's law.
For all wisdom is the fear of God, and all wisdom carries out his law.
There is no wisdom that teaches evil, and there is no wisdom in the counsel of the wicked and sinners.
There is an evil more defiling than all others, and there is a fool who lacks understanding.
But it is better to be a fool and fear God than to be clever and reject God's law.
There is someone who acts cleverly and cautiously while doing wrong. There is someone who twists counsel and makes a show of favoring his neighbor and securing a just judgment for his friend.
There is someone who favors evil without praising it, yet his heart is full of deceit.
There is someone who flatters you to your face while something else is in his heart, and he comes upon you when you do not expect him.
Even if his strength fails and he cannot harm you, [?] he will lead you astray into an action that will hurt you.
For a person is known by his appearance, and a wise person is known by his face.
A person's character is known by his clothing, his walk, and his laughter.
There is someone who rebukes, but not for a good purpose, and there is someone who remains silent because he is wise.
It is better to rebuke than to bear a grudge. There is someone who confesses because his sin has overcome him.
Like a eunuch who desires to deflower a virgin is someone who desires to impose judgment by force.
There is someone who knows but remains silent, and there is someone who makes himself hated by talking too much.
There is someone who remains silent because he does not know what to answer, and there is someone who remains silent until he finds the right moment.
A wise man remains silent until he finds the right moment, but a fool and an insolent person speak whenever they have the chance.
People are annoyed with someone who talks too much, and they hate someone who exalts himself.
There is a person whose poverty leads him astray [?], and there is someone who gains something but cannot keep it.
There is someone who gives you something and then demands twice as much back from you.
There is someone who exalts himself while poor, and there is someone who gains honor by humbling himself.
There is someone who sells much for little and seeks to make it sevenfold.
A wise person wins acceptance through his words, but the gifts of fools bring no favor.
A fool gives something of no value. Even if he gives only a little, he thinks in his heart that he has given you much.

Even if he gives you only a little, he insults you as though he had given you much. He speaks arrogantly against you and goes around telling you what he gave you. If he gives you something today, he demands it back tomorrow. Such a person is hateful.
The fool says that he does not want a friend: “What good does it do me? For he receives no reward for the good I have done. Even those who eat my bread speak cruelly against you.”
And they all continually slander me and laugh at me.
It is better to slip and fall on the ground than to slip with your mouth and fall through your tongue. In the same way, the fall of the wicked comes swiftly.
Someone who speaks whatever comes to him disgraces himself, and his words find no favor. In the mouths of fools, speech goes astray.
A proverb falls flat in a fool’s mouth, because he does not tell it at the proper time.
There is one who turns to the fear of God from the time he is conceived, and his soul will rest in well-being.
There is someone who destroys his own life out of shame and throws his life away through his foolishness.
There is someone who, out of shame, gives hope to the person before whom he feels ashamed, without giving anything. Because of this, he needlessly makes him an enemy.
Terrible is the disgrace of a lying man; the speech of fools goes astray.
A thief is better than a liar, but the end of both is death and disgrace.
For a lying person suffers disgrace and is continually put to shame.
Someone who is wise in speech will have his words heard, and a wise man strengthens his rulers.
Someone who works the land increases his heap of grain, and someone who serves his rulers benefits himself.
Gifts and bribes blind the eyes of the wise, shut their mouths, and turn their words aside.
Hidden wisdom is like buried treasure. What use is either of them?
A fool who hides his foolishness is better than a wise man who buries his wisdom.
My son, if you have sinned and gone astray, do not do it again. Stop, then, and plead for forgiveness for your former wrongdoing.
Just as someone flees from a dangerous snake, so flee from sin. If it wounds you, it will not let you escape. Its teeth are like a lion’s teeth, and it destroys human life.
Every sin is like a sharp, double-edged razor, and wherever it wounds, there is no healing for its wound.
Insolence, boasting, and arrogance ruin a rich man; likewise, the house of the proud is ruined.
When a poor man pleads, his plea is brought to his ears, and his cry reaches him swiftly.
Someone who hates correction follows sinners, but someone who fears God changes his heart when he is corrected.
Someone who can speak well is recognized from afar, but a wise man recognizes when he goes astray.
Someone who builds his house with borrowed money builds it like a wall in the rainy season.
The gathering of sinners is like a heap of straw, and in the end they will become fuel for a blazing fire.
The stones of the path of sinners are [?], and its end is a precipice.
Whoever strengthens his heart keeps the law of the Lord, and wisdom follows the fear of the Lord.
Someone who has not been instructed will not become wise. Yet there is someone who receives instruction, and his disgrace increases.
The understanding of a wise person is abundant like floodwater, and his counsel gushes forth like living water.
A fool's mind is like a broken jar; it cannot retain anything it hears.
When a person of understanding hears a wise saying, he praises it and adds further to it. But when an evil-minded person hears it, he vomits it out and throws it behind his back.
A fool's speech is like a heavy burden on a long journey, but grace is beautiful on the lips of the wise.
The voice of a wise person is heard in the assembly, and his words enter the heart.
Wisdom among fools is like a ruined house, and a fool's counsel is unwanted speech.
Instruction is to fools like shackles on the feet; and a fool's constrained mind is like someone whose right hand is bound.
When a fool laughs, he raises his voice, but a wise person smiles with his lips in wonder.
Wisdom is like a gold necklace to a discerning person, and like a bracelet on the right hand.
A fool's foot quickly enters a house, but a man who has suffered in every way lowers his face in shame.
A fool peers through the door into another person's house, but a wise man stands outside.
You can hear a person's foolishness from outside, but a wise person despises it greatly.
To a stranger this matter is astonishing; the words of the wise are fittingly arranged.
Fools have their hearts in their mouths, and the counsel of the wise is the speech of their mouths.
When a sinner curses a demon, he curses his own soul.
A slanderer defiles his own soul and makes himself hated wherever he lives.
A lazy person is like a filthy stone wherever he sits, and everyone hisses at him because of his shameful laziness.
A lazy person is like discarded dung wherever he lies; everyone who picks it up shakes it off his hand.
A foolish son is a disgrace to his father, and a foolish daughter becomes a source of dishonor.
A wise daughter will obtain a husband, but one who brings shame is a sorrow to the woman who bore her.
An arrogant woman who is [?] in every respect disgraces both her father and her husband and is despised.
Someone who speaks wherever he happens to be is like those who provide food in a house of mourning. Whipping and correction make a person wise at all times.
Teaching a fool is like gluing broken pottery together, like waking a sleeper from a deep sleep.
Likewise, speaking to a fool is like speaking to someone asleep. When you have finished speaking, he says to you, "What did you say?"

Weep for the dead, because his light has passed away; and weep for a fool, because his understanding has deserted him. It is right to weep for the dead, because there is no return. But weep for a fool throughout his life, because being alive is worse for him than being dead.

Do not talk much with a fool, and do not travel with someone who has no understanding. Be on your guard so that he does not bring you into trouble and so that you are not [?] by his foolishness. Keep away from him, and your soul will find rest and relief; you will suffer no harm from his foolishness.
What is heavier than lead? And what is its name but a fool?
It is better to carry sand, salt, and a weight of iron than to live with a fool.
A well-fitted bond secured within a masonry wall will not come loose even if it is shaken. So it is with wise counsel within a steadfast heart.
The defenses of a steadfast heart and wise counsel will never be broken down. It is like a layer of sand within a resting place.
Like straw before a storm, which cannot stand when the wind comes, so are foolish thoughts within a fearful heart: they cannot stand when something frightens it.
Whoever pokes an eye makes tears flow, and whoever probes a heart brings wisdom to light.
Whoever throws stones at birds drives them away, and whoever insults his friend destroys his friendship.
Even if you have drawn a sword against your friend.

Even if you have spoken arrogantly against him, do not give up on him, for he may be reconciled to you. But if you insult him, speak arrogantly against him, mock him, disclose his secrets, deal treacherously with him, and hurt him, every friend will flee because of such behavior.

Even if you are poor, remain faithful to your companion, so that you may rejoice when he rejoices. Even if he is oppressed, endure with him, so that you may rejoice with him when he receives his inheritance.
Smoke and vapor rise before a fire; likewise, abuse and quarreling come before bloodshed.
I am not ashamed to shelter my friend, and I do not hide from his presence.
And if harm befalls me because of him, everyone who hears of it will guard himself against him.
Who will set a guard over my mouth for me, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, so that I may not fall through it and my tongue may not kill me?
Lord, my Father, God of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel, and do not let me fall through them.
Who will discipline my heart for me, and who will teach wisdom to my mind, so that my folly may leave me and they may not overcome me by what they say against me?
So that my errors may not multiply, my sin may not increase, and I may not fall before my adversaries, nor my enemies rejoice over me.
My Lord and Father, God of my life, do not bring me anything that leads my eyes astray.
And lessen the desire within us.
Do not let gluttony come upon me or lust overpower me, and do not hand me over to evil desire.
Listen, my children, to the instruction of my mouth. Whoever observes it and keeps his lips under control will not slip.
The sinner, the arrogant, and the scoffer are ensnared by them.
My child, do not accustom your mouth to swearing oaths, and do not mention the name of the Holy One when you swear.
Just as a servant who is constantly interrogated never lacks wounds on his body, so someone who continually mentions the name of God while swearing will not be free from sin.

A man who swears has many offenses, and punishment will never cease from his house. Even if he forgets, his sin will not leave him; and if he turns a deaf ear, his guilt will be doubled. He will not be acquitted for what he swore, for his punishment falls fully upon his house.
There is speech that brings death; may it not be found in Jacob’s inheritance. None of this is found among the righteous, and they will not be ensnared in sin.
Let no mocking words come out of your mouth, for there is much sin in them.

Remember your father and mother, and associate with your rulers. Do not go astray before them or disgrace yourself through your folly, so that you do not say, “If only I had not been born,” or curse the day you were born.
A man accustomed to mockery will not become wise as long as he lives.

There are two things that lead to sin, and a third that leads to the loss of life: rage that burns like fire and does not cool until it overwhelms him; and a man who commits sexual immorality through his bodily desire does not stop until he kindles the fire.
To an adulterous man, every kind of food tastes sweet, and he will not rest until he dies.

A man who strays from his own bed says in his heart, “No one sees me. The darkness of the land and the walls hide me. What, then, should I fear? No one knows me, and the Most High will forget my sins and will not remember me.”

He fears only human eyes, lest they see him, and does not know that the eyes of the Lord shine brighter than myriads of suns. They see all the deeds of human beings and know everything done in secret.
He will punish him in the middle of the city and catch him where he did not expect it.
So too a woman who leaves her husband and bears an heir by a lover.
First, she has denied God; second, she has betrayed her husband; and third, she has stolen through her adultery and borne children by a lover.
They will disgrace such a woman, and she will be punished through her children.
Her offspring and her fruit will [?], and her branches will bear no fruit.
Her memory will be cursed, and she will leave a curse to her household. Her curse and disgrace will never end.
Then everyone who sees her will know that nothing is better than fearing the Lord, and nothing is sweeter than keeping the Lord’s commandments.
Wisdom praises herself and boasts among her people.
In the assembly of the Most High she opens her mouth and boasts before his host.
I came forth from the mouth of the Most High and covered the earth like mist.
I dwelt in the heavens, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.
Alone I circled the farthest reaches of heaven and walked in the depths of the abyss,
over the waves of the sea and throughout the whole earth. I gained possessions among all nations and among all peoples.
After all this I sought a resting place. In whose inheritance, then, should I dwell?
Then the Creator of all commanded me, and my Creator established a resting place for me. He said to me, “Dwell in Jacob, and receive your inheritance in Israel.”
Before the world was created, he created me, and he will never perish, for ever and ever.
I served before him in his holy tabernacle, and I was established in Zion.
Likewise I rested in the holy city, and my dominion was in Jerusalem, where he appointed me to rule.
I put down roots among an honored people, in the Lord’s portion and in his inheritance.
I rose high like a cedar in Lebanon, like a cedar in the mountains of Hermon.
I grew tall like a palm tree at the water’s edge, like a rose in Jericho, and like a beautiful olive tree in the wilderness. I grew large like a plane tree.
My fragrance was sweet like cinnamon and aspalathus. My fragrance was like the scent of choice myrrh, like galbanum, onycha, and stacte, and like the smoke of incense in the tabernacle.
My branches spread out like a terebinth, and my branches were branches of honor and praise.
Like a vine, I put forth grace, and my blossoms are the fruit of honor (and glory) and wealth.
Come to me, all of you who desire me, and eat your fill of my grain.
For the memory of me is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance is sweeter than sugar.
Those who eat me will not have enough of me, and those who drink me will not be satisfied with me.
Whoever listens to me will not be put to shame, and those who serve me will not go astray.
All this is the message of the book of the law of the Most High, the law that Moses commanded as an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
It makes wisdom overflow like the River Pishon, and like the River Tigris in the months of [?].
It makes counsel overflow like the River Euphrates, and like the River Jordan at harvest time.
He reveals wisdom like light, and like the river Gihon in the days of the grape harvest.
The first did not fully comprehend her, and the last did not discover her tracks.
Her thoughts are more abundant than the waters of the sea, and her counsel is deeper than the waters of the abyss.
I became like a stream of water flowing out of a river, and like an irrigation channel I entered a garden.
I said, “I will water the garden and soak my vegetable beds.” Then this stream of mine became like a river, and my river became as large as the sea.
Again I will make wisdom shine like the dawn, and I will make her visible far away.
I will pour out instruction like prophecy, and I will leave it for generation after generation, forever and ever.
Look and see that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek me.
With these three things I am adorned, and I stand beautiful before God and humanity: brothers united in heart, friendship between companions, and a husband and wife united in their way of life.
My soul rejects and hates three worthless kinds of people, and their lives anger me even more: an arrogant poor person, a rich liar, and an adulterous old man without sense.
If you were not disciplined in your youth, how will you become wise in your old age?
Sound judgment is fitting for gray hair, and counsel is fitting for the learned.
Wisdom is fitting for the aged, and instruction in wisdom is fitting for elders.
The crown of the aged is abundant learning, and their pride is the fear of God.
There are nine whom I have called blessed in my heart, and I will speak of ten with my mouth: a man who rejoices in his children, and who, while still alive, sees the downfall of his enemy.
Blessed is the man who marries a wise wife, and blessed is the one who does not stumble in his speech and who does not come under someone worse than himself.
Blessed is the one who finds wisdom and who finds someone who obeys him.
Great is the one who finds wisdom, but the one who fears God is greater than he.
The fear of God is better than everything, and whoever keeps it has no equal.
A wound of the heart is worse than every other wound, and a woman's wickedness is worse than every other wickedness.
Even if you fall into every other misfortune, do not fall into the hands of your enemy. Even if everyone else takes revenge on you, may your enemy not take revenge on you.
No head is worse than the head of a snake, and no resentment is worse than an enemy’s resentment.
It is better to live with lions and wild beasts of the earth than to live with an evil woman.
Her wickedness changes his appearance and makes his face dark like a bear’s.
Among his companions they mock her husband, afflict him with bitter grief, and make him groan.
Every evil is small compared with a woman’s evil; she brings one into a share of sin.
As a sandy slope exhausts the feet of the elderly, so a talkative woman exhausts a gentle man.
Do not let a woman’s beauty lead you astray, and do not let a woman’s beauty entice you.
For it is (a scourge and) humiliation and great disgrace, and also shame, if a wife supports her husband.
An evil woman is a wound to the heart, darkness to the face, and sorrow to the soul. Like a crippled hand and a lame foot is a wife who does not praise her husband.
Sin first came from a woman, and because of her we all die.
Do not make a channel for water, and do not show a woman what is in your heart.
If she does not conform to your disposition, cut her off from yourself and separate her from your flesh.
The husband of a good woman is blessed, and the days of his life will be doubled.
A strong woman makes her husband happy, and he completes his days in peace.
A good woman is a good portion, and she falls to the lot of the man who fears God.
Whether rich or poor, his heart is content. Let your face always be bright.
My heart was startled by these three things, and a fourth made my face tremble: slander throughout a city, a gathering of crowds, and false testimony against a person that leads to death.
A jealous woman is a wound to the heart and anguish to the soul; like a scourging tongue, she matches every evil.
An evil woman is like an ox’s yoke that shakes loose, and whoever lives with her is like someone holding a scorpion.
A drunken woman is a great cause of anger; she cannot cover her shame.
A woman’s sexual immorality is recognized by her eyes and known by her eyelids.
Keep a strict watch over your daughter if she goes astray, so that she does not ruin herself.
Beware of a wandering eye, so that you do not later regret it if someone wrongs you.
Like a thirsty person who laps and drinks from any water nearby, he takes shelter beneath every tree, like someone drawing his arrow from his quiver.
A woman's grace makes her husband happy, and her wisdom refreshes his bones.
A gentle woman is pleasing to God, and a wise soul is beyond price.
A modest woman is goodness added to blessing, and a patient soul has no substitute.
Like the sun in God’s heaven is the radiant beauty of a good woman in the structure of her house.
Like a holy lamp shining on its stand is the radiance of a wise man’s face in the beauty of his disposition.
Like golden pillars standing on silver steps is the footing of a good man who stands firm in goodness.

These three things grieved my heart, and the fourth brought anger upon me: a fighting (and courageous) man when he is in want and [?]; wise men when they go astray; and someone who abandons righteousness and returns to sin—God will bring him down by the sword.
Only with difficulty does a trader escape sin, and a merchant is not free from wrongdoing.
Many commit sin through partiality, and whoever wants to grow rich turns his eyes away.
A peg is driven between stones in a wall, and sin comes between selling and buying.
If a person is not quick to guard himself in the fear of God, the overthrow of his house will not be delayed.
Chaff falls through a sieve; likewise, a person's impurity is discovered through his thoughts.
Fire tests the potter's vessels, and the thoughts of a person's heart test him.
The one who tends grain sees its fruit; likewise, a person's words reveal the desire of his heart.
Do not praise a person before questioning him, for speech puts a person to the test.
If you pursue righteousness, you will find it and wear it like a splendid full-length robe.
A bird settles with its own kind, and righteousness goes to those who practice it.
A lion hunts for something to eat; likewise, sin hunts those who practice it.
The righteous person always teaches wisdom, but the fool's heart wanes like the morning moon.
Among fools, watch your time; among the wise, ask questions at all times.
The talk of fools provokes anger, and their laughter is sinful revelry.
The speech of someone who swears often makes the hair stand on end, and their quarrels deafen the ears.
The quarrels of the arrogant spill blood, and their speech is a burden to those who hear them.
Whoever reveals his companion's secret destroys their trust and will no longer find a friend after his own heart.
Protect your friend and be faithful to him. But if you have revealed his secret, do not pursue him (then, and do not follow) behind him.
Just as a person destroys his enemy, so you too have destroyed your brotherly bond with your friend.
Like a bird that escapes from your hand, your friend has flown away from you.
Do not pursue him any longer, for he has escaped far from you, like a gazelle escaping from a snare.
If it is a wound, they can heal it; if someone has been insulted, they can reconcile him. But whoever reveals his companion's secret will be abandoned.
The person who winks his eye has no good intention; no one can make him abandon his evil.
To your face his mouth speaks pleasantly to you, and he praises you for everything you say. But afterward he changes what he says to you and trips you up with the very words you spoke.
There are many whom I have hated, but none like him; God also hates him.
Whoever throws a stone upward will have it fall on his own head; the wound from an unjust blow will become known.
Whoever digs a pit for his companion will fall into it himself, and whoever sets a trap will be caught in it.
Sin insults and mocks the arrogant; like a lion it bites them and takes vengeance on them.
Those who rejoice at the fall of the righteous will be caught in a trap. Scourges will destroy them before the time of their death arrives.
Wrath and anger are unclean things, and they dwell with a sinful person.
Whoever waits patiently for the Lord, the Lord will avenge him and forgive his sin.
Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then, when you pray, your sins will be forgiven.
When you, being human, bear a grudge against another person (someone like yourself), how can you then say to the Lord, “Have mercy on me”?
When you show no mercy to someone like yourself, how can you ask him to forgive your sins?
Remember your end and abandon hatred. Remember death and decay, and keep his commandments.
Remember his law and do not bear a grudge against your neighbor. Remember the judgment of the Most High and let go of anger.
Restrain a quarrel, and you will lessen your sins. An angry person makes strife boil.
A sinful person troubles his neighbor and stirs up discord among friends.

The more wood a fire has, the greater its blaze; the greater a quarrel grows, the more fiercely its strife boils. A person's resentment is in proportion to his strength, and in proportion to his wealth he increases his anger.
Whoever persists in his arrogance kindles a fire, and whoever stirs up a quarrel hastens the shedding of blood.
If you blow on a coal, it burns; if you spit on it, it goes out. Both come out of the mouth.
People curse the slanderer and the double-tongued person, because he has made many friends fight one another.
A tongue that stirs up discord has troubled many and driven them from nation to nation. It has destroyed fortified cities and brought down the houses of the powerful.
A gossiping tongue has driven women from their husbands' homes and destroyed the fruits of their labor.
Whoever does not guard himself will never find rest and will not live in peace.
A wound from a whip produces pus, but a wound from the tongue breaks bones.
Many have fallen by the sword, but not as many as have fallen by the tongue.
Blessed is the person who has escaped it, who has not slipped on its slippery ground, who has not plowed under its yoke, and who has not been bound in its chains.
Her yoke is an iron yoke, and her shackles are bronze.
The death it brings is a terrible death; Sheol is easier than it.
But it will not reach the righteous, and they will not be burned by its fire.
Those who forget the Lord will fall into it, and it will burn them with an unquenchable fire. It will spring upon them like a lion and seize them like a leopard.
Even if you have fenced your possessions with thorns and sealed up your gold and silver,
You have weighed your words on a balance and placed a door and a bolt over your mouth.
guard your tongue as well, so that it does not make you stumble and you do not fall before the one who lies in wait for you.
Someone who gives charity lends to his neighbor, and someone who has enough at hand carries out his commandment.
Lend to your neighbor when he is in need, so that you may prosper with him when he prospers.
Keep your word and be faithful to him, and when you wish, you will find him because of your righteousness.
Many regard borrowed money as something they have found on the ground, and they cause trouble for those who lent to them and helped them in their distress.

Until he has borrowed, he kisses your head, lowers his voice, and treats you gently until he takes your money. But when you ask him to repay, he prolongs the time, repays you with bitterness and quarrels instead of your money, and wears out (and lets pass) your time.

If he repays even half, it is a remarkable thing, and even that will seem to you like something you found on the ground. Otherwise, you suffer the loss, and he also becomes your enemy. He repays you with curses and quarrels, and dishonors you instead of honoring you.
Many do not lend because of a friend's unwillingness, and out of fear that they may suffer loss or be hated.
But be patient with the poor, and do not withhold charity from them.
For the sake of charity, receive the poor person, and because he is in distress, do not send him away empty-handed.
Lose your gold rather than lose your friend and your neighbor, and rather than let it rust in a storehouse and be lost beneath a stone.
Spend what you have stored up, in obedience to the commandment of the Most High, and it will benefit you more than treasuries of gold.
Store up charity in your houses, and it will be better able to save you from all your distress.
More readily than a spear or a weapon of war, it will go before you, defeat your enemy for you, and fight your adversary for you.
A good man stands surety for his friend, but a shameless man turns a blind eye.
Do not forget to repay the person who stood surety for you, for he offered his life in your place.
A wicked person brings a good guarantor to ruin.
A sinner forgets to repay the person who saved him.
Standing surety has brought suffering upon many good people and tossed them about like the waves of the sea. It has brought strong men to ruin and driven them into exile among foreign nations.
A sinner impoverishes himself by giving a pledge, and whoever is greedy for profit falls into loss.
Support your neighbor according to your ability, but guard yourself so that he does not bring you to ruin.
The first necessities of your life are food, water, clothing, and a house where you can conceal your nakedness.
It is better to be poor beneath the beams of your own house than to prosper and live proudly in someone else’s house, with another person’s possessions.
Make your conduct and your speech pleasing to both the lowly and the great.
The life of someone who moves from house to house is miserable. Wherever you stay, be cautious and do not speak boldly.
Otherwise, even if you provide food and drink, you receive no thanks, and on top of all this they speak bitter words to you.
When you are prosperous, they say to you, “Come in, our guest! Set the table and feed us with what you have.”
But once you become poor, they say to you, “Go away, our guest! Our relative has arrived; we need our house.”
This is a terrible thing in the eyes of a wise man: the person who has housed you dishonors you, and the person who has lent to you harasses you.
Whoever loves his son does not withhold discipline, so that he may rejoice in him in the end.
People praise the man who has taught his son because of him, and his son becomes his source of pride among his relatives.
Someone who teaches his son makes his enemy jealous and rejoices in his son among his friends.
Even if his father dies, it is as though he has not died, because he has left someone like himself behind.
While he is alive, he rejoices in his son, and even when he dies, his heart is not troubled.
For after him there remains someone who will take revenge on his enemies and repay his friends.
Harden your heart toward your children's feelings, for their crying will stir your compassion.
An untrained horse turns out badly, and an undisciplined son turns out insolent.
If you joke with your son, he will become overbearing toward you; if you play with him, he will cause you pain.
Do not laugh with him, lest he bring you sorrow and make you grind your teeth in the end.
Do not give your son authority in his youth.
While he is young, strike the bones of his ribs, so that when he grows strong he will not rebel against you.
Teach your son, and he will give you authority, so that you will not be ashamed of his corruption.
A poor person who is healthy and free in spirit is better off than a rich person whose body is sick and whose spirit is bound.
May your body be healthy and your spirit free: this is better than all wealth. A healthy soul is better than all wealth and possessions.
Wealth does not surpass a healthy life, and no pleasure is better than a joyful heart.
Death is better than a bitter life or a wasting disease.
Like food poured into a closed mouth is food laid out on graves.
What good is a sacrifice to gods? They cannot smell it. So it is with someone whom God has afflicted.
He sees with his eyes, and his heart aches, like a eunuch who embraces a virgin and grieves.
Do not bring sorrow upon yourself or trouble your heart.
