A joyful heart is a person's life, and gladness of soul lengthens one's days.
Be gentle with yourself and comfort your heart, so that you may drive sorrow away from you. For sorrow has killed many, and sorrow brings no benefit.
Jealousy and anger shorten the days of life, and grief makes a person old before their time.
Like one who gleans after the grape gatherer, I succeeded through the Lord's blessing; like a grape harvester, I filled my winepress.
Look and see that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who wish to become wise.
Listen to me, rulers of the people, and give me your attention, leaders of the nations.

Do not give your son, your wife, your brother, or your friend authority over your property while you are alive. Do not appoint a stranger over your household, lest you later regret it and have to plead with them.
As long as you are alive and have breath in you, do not surrender your independence.
It is better for your children to ask you for things than for you to look to your children for support.
Be wise in everything you do, and do not disgrace yourself in the position to which you have been appointed.
When the days of your life come to an end and your final hour arrives, then hand over your property as an inheritance.
Feed a donkey, load it, and beat it; likewise, discipline a servant, feed him, and put him to work.
Put your servants to work, and you will find rest; but if you leave them idle, they will rebel (they will want to leave you).
A harnessed yoke bends the neck, and a whip and shackles are for an unruly servant.
Put your servant to work, and do not leave him idle.
For idleness teaches much evil.
Give him work according to his strength, and if he does not obey, make his shackles heavier. Do not trust everyone of flesh, and do nothing without counsel.
If you have a servant living with you (a good one), treat him like your brother and love him as yourself.
If you have been harsh toward him and done wrong, he will turn you back. By what road, then, will you seek him?
A foolish man vainly longs for falsehood, and dreams terrify a fool.
Like someone grasping a shadow or chasing the wind is someone who trusts a dream.
A dream shifts from one thing to another, and shows you each thing in the likeness of its own appearance.
What clean thing can come from something unclean? And where can truth be found in falsehood?
Dreams, omens, and divination are all empty. They disturb the heart and torment it like labor pains.
Unless it was sent from God when he shows mercy, do not take it to heart.
For dreams have led many astray, and they have fallen while putting their hope in them.
What comes from God is surely fulfilled, without falsehood, and the word of truth is confirmed.
A man trained by discipline knows much, and one who has suffered greatly pours out wisdom.
But one who has suffered no harm knows nothing.
One who has undergone many hardships gains much discernment.
I saw much when I underwent hardships, and my words exceeded my understanding.
For I continually undergo hardships and come close to death, and because of this God saves me.
The soul that fears God will live.
And all who put their hope in him will be saved.
Nothing terrifies the one who fears God, and he will not be alarmed, because God is his hope.
Blessed is the soul that fears God.
For he leans on him, and he is his refuge.

The eyes of God are on those who love him. His strength is trustworthy, and his support is firm. He cools the heat for you and shades you from the midday sun. He guards you against stumbling and helps you against falling.
He strengthens your soul and brightens your eyes; he also heals, gives life, and provides abundant blessing.
A sacrifice offered from unjust gains is unclean, and the offering of sinners is abhorrent.
He will not accept the offerings of the wicked.
Your sins will not be forgiven because of the abundance of your offerings.
Someone who brings an offering from wealth gained through injustice is like someone who kills a child in front of his father.
The life of a poor person depends on begging for alms, and whoever refuses him is a murderer.
Whoever separates a man from his wife is like someone who kills his neighbor.
Whoever withholds a laborer’s wages sheds his blood.
When one person builds and another tears down, what benefit do the two gain from their labor?
When one person prays and another curses, whose voice will he hear out of the two?
If someone washes after touching a corpse and then touches it again, what benefit has he gained from washing?
So it is with someone who fasts because of his sins and then goes and sins again. Who, then, will hear his prayer, and what benefit has he gained from afflicting himself?
Whoever keeps his law brings an offering.
Whoever heeds his commandment offers a sacrifice for his salvation.
Whoever brings fine flour repays a kindness.
Whoever gives alms offers a sacrifice of praise.
The Lord’s will is that you do no evil, and what pleases him is that you turn away from injustice.
Do not come before the Lord empty-handed.
Do all this because of his commandment.
The sacrifice of a righteous person covers the altar, and its fragrance reaches the Most High.
The sacrifice of a righteous person is holy, and its remembrance will not be forgotten before him.
Praise the Lord with a cheerful look, and do not neglect to bring an offering from the firstfruits of your labor.
With every gift you give him, let your face be cheerful, and bring the tithe of your labor with joy.
Bring an offering to the Lord in keeping with the thanks due to him, and offer generously to him from what you have in your hands.
For the Lord repays, and he will reward you sevenfold.
Do not bring him deceit, for he will not accept it from you.
Do not think that you can bribe him with an unjust offering, for the Lord is a righteous judge and shows no partiality.
He will not show partiality against the poor, and he will hear the cry of the oppressed.
He will not turn a deaf ear to the orphan’s prayer or to a widowed woman when someone makes her weep.
She has shed tears upon her cheeks.
Likewise, he will bring cries of distress upon the one who made her weep.
He accepts the one who serves him in righteousness, and that person’s prayer rises as far as the clouds.
The prayer of the poor passes through the clouds and does not turn back until it reaches its destination; it does not withdraw until the Lord sees it.
He will give justice to the righteous and avenge them. The Lord will not delay over them or remain patient on their account until he crushes their enemies’ loins.
He will take vengeance on the nations, destroy all the unjust, and break the staff of sinners.
He will repay every person according to their deeds, and all mortals according to their deeds and their ways.
He will do this until he has avenged his people and made them rejoice in his mercy.
Blessed is the one who finds mercy in the days of suffering, like a rain cloud over parched land.
Have mercy on us, Lord, God of all power, and turn toward us.
Send the fear of you upon all nations.
Raise your hand against a foreign people, and let them see your power.
Just as you showed your holiness among us while they watched, so show your glory among them while we watch.
They too will know you as we have known you, for there is no God besides you, Lord.
Show your signs and reveal your glory,
through the power of your hand and the majesty of your right hand.
Bring destruction and send a plague.
Destroy the oppressor and crush the enemy.
Remember their oath and hasten their day. [?]
Strike them with wrath and fire, and destroy those who have escaped from among them. Let death overtake those who have treated your people cruelly.
Break the heads of the enemy’s messengers, who say, “There is no one besides us.”
Gather together all the descendants of Jacob.
They will not reject a good heart or tasty food. Keeping watch over wealth wears out bones and soul, and concern for possessions drives sleep away.
Anxious vigilance puts an end to sleep. During deep slumber, sickness keeps one awake, and there is no sleep.
The rich man goes about gathering wealth, and when he rests, he revels in abundance.
The poor man works for lack of possessions, and when he rests, he returns to begging.
One who loves wealth will not be righteous, and one who loves sin will follow it.
Many have fallen because of wealth and have seen their death before their eyes.
It is a stumbling block to all who seek it, and every fool stumbles over it.
Blessed is the rich person who is free from sin and whose heart does not pursue wealth.
Who is he? Let us call him blessed, for he has done good among his people.
Who has been tested by it and has not gone astray? He has become a source of pride. Who could have done evil but did not, and who could have committed sin but did not?
May his blessing endure, and may his acts of charity be heard of among the people.
When you sit at a lavish table, do not open your mouth wide over it, and do not say, “They have set out a great deal on it.”
Remember that the human eye is evil. What is more evil than the eye of a mortal? That is why the eye sheds tears.
Do not be greedy for everything you see, and do not let your hands be grasping. Do not search through the bowls or lick the platters.
Recognize that your neighbor has given you a meal, and consider everything he has set before you.
Eat what has been set before you like a wise person. Do not gobble as you chew, lest you disgust your neighbor.
Be the first to stop, like a wise person. Do not be greedy or act like someone who cannot get enough.
If you are sitting among many people, do not be the first to reach out your hands.
Eat in moderation, like a wise person who is satisfied with a little, and your breathing will not be labored in bed.

The person who restrains his appetite sleeps soundly, and when he wakes in the morning, his breathing is not troubled. But the greedy person who cannot get enough suffers from cramps, vomiting, and abdominal pain.
If they make you eat, get up before them and rest.
Listen to me, my son, and do not disregard my instruction. Later you will understand my words. Do not be careless in anything you do, so that you do not go wrong in anything.
They follow the generous person because of his good conduct. [?]
The miser is cursed because of his evil character. [?]
Do not boast about how much you have drunk, for drinking has led many astray.
Strong iron is tested in the furnace; in the same way, wine tests the hearts of the proud.
Drinking wine is life to a person, and it is a joy to anyone who drinks it in moderation. What is life to someone who does not drink wine? For it was created for the enjoyment of mortals.
Drinking good wine in moderation and at the proper time brings gladness to the heart and joy to the soul.
Wine makes the heart forget its sorrow. Give wine to the weary and to those who are sad.
When a fool drinks, he increases his [?], goes astray, and makes mistakes. Heavy drinking brings no strength and never fails to bring wounds.

Do not rebuke your neighbor while he is drinking wine, and do not distress him while his heart is glad. Do not tell him [?], do not harass him, and do not appeal to him about your troubles while he is drunk.
If they appoint you leader, do not exalt yourself. Be like them, as one of them; attend to their concerns, and sit down.
Govern them so that you may receive a crown of honor when you have completed your service.
Speak, old man, for it is fitting for you. Do not remain silent when you have something good to say, teaching your wisdom.
Do not make your voice heard to everyone who questions you, and do not display your wisdom whenever you have the chance.
Like a precious jewel in a gold setting is singing where people drink wine.
Like an emerald in a gold ring is the sweetness of singing and the lyre in a house where people drink.
Speak, young man, if they allow you. Speak sparingly when they ask you a second time.
Once you have answered, bring your speech to an end. Even though you know, keep your mouth silent.
Do not sit among the great, and do not make your voice heard while someone else is speaking.
As lightning flashes before thunder, so favor goes before the face of a modest person.
Do everything at its proper time and in due measure. Go into your house and rejoice there.
Enjoy yourself and do all the pleasant things you desire. Take care not to speak arrogantly or give offense with your words.
Along with all this, give thanks to your Creator, and he will satisfy you with all his blessings.
Whoever fears the Lord will praise his discipline, and those who go to him will find what they desire.
Whoever seeks his law will be satisfied by it, but whoever doubts it will fall and go astray.
He will give judgment in favor of those who fear the Lord, and at midday he will avenge the wrongs done to them.
But a sinful man does not listen to those who correct him, and in his heart he thinks everyone is like himself.
A wise man does nothing without advice. But a [?] and arrogant man who is troubled by fear acts without advice.
But you, my son, do nothing without advice, and do not ruin what you have accomplished.
Do not travel a desolate road, lest you stumble over stones.
Do not trust your enemy in the open country.
Do not trust even your son if he does not follow your ways.
In everything you do, gladden your soul, and in everything keep his commandments.
Whoever fears the law listens to the commandment of the book, and whoever trusts in the Lord will not go astray.
No evil will befall anyone who fears the Lord except to test him, and he will escape from it.
A wise man loves to hear Scripture read, but whoever doubts and does not trust his Scripture will be like a ship tossing in the midst of a storm.
A wise man trusts and rejoices in the Lord’s law, and the Lord will be his support and make him glad.
Prepare yourself, you who speak; make your voice heard. Gather your thoughts and give an answer about what you will do.
A fool’s heart is like a chariot wheel, and a fearful person’s counsel is like a revolving axle.
A [?] horse is like a good friend.
Why is one day longer than another, when all the days of the year pass in the light of the sun?
By the Lord’s command all the days are distinguished, and the times of his festivals are known by his reckoning.
Among the days there are some that he made holy and exalted. From among them he distinguished winter, harvest, and summer, each according to its reckoning and its season.
All of us human beings are from the earth, and Adam was created from the ground.
The Lord distinguished them in the abundance of his wisdom and established their paths.
Some among them he blessed and exalted; some among them he made holy and appeared to them; and some among them he cursed, humbled, and cast out according to their deeds.
Like clay in the potter’s hands, so are we before him, and all his work follows his ways. So too a human being is in the hands of his Creator, and he repays everyone according to their deeds.
Good is the opposite of evil, and life is the opposite of death. Likewise, the sinner is the opposite of the righteous person.
And with all this, look at the work of the Most High: everything comes in pairs, [?] each with its counterpart.
As for me, after I had considered this and investigated it from the beginning.
Have mercy, Lord, on your people who are called by your name, and on Israel, whom you likened to your firstborn.
Have mercy on the city of your sanctuary, and on Jerusalem, the city where you dwell and rest.
Fill Zion with the blessing of your word, and let your glory be upon your people.
Give your law to your earliest creatures, and establish prophets for your name.
Give their reward to those who have hoped in you, so that people may believe your prophets.
Hear, Lord, the prayer of your prophets and your servants. Send Aaron’s blessing upon your people, and let everyone who lives on earth know that you are the Lord, the eternal God.
All food is eaten and goes down into the stomach, but some food tastes better than other food.
The palate distinguishes every taste of food; likewise, a wise person’s heart distinguishes false speech.
An evil heart brings sorrow, and a man who has suffered much is taught by his endurance.
Every man takes a wife, but one woman may be better than another.
A woman’s beauty brightens the face; she surpasses everything a man desires.
And if she is gentle and her speech is good, her husband is unlike other men.
A man who marries a good woman has found his delight, for she is his helper and the pillar on which he leans.
Like someone who gains nothing and whose belongings are stolen, so a man without a wife lives in poverty.
Who would trust a thief who moves from town to town? So it is with a man who has no children and no settled home, who spends the night wherever evening overtakes him.
Everyone who befriends you says, “I too am your friend.” But there is someone who befriends you who is a friend in name only.
Sorrow remains in the heart until the day of death, and there is a friend who becomes your enemy.
Evil desire, where did you roll in from and fill the land with sin?
There is a friend who comes close to you when you are happy, but when you are in distress he becomes your enemy.
There is a friend who grieves over your suffering for the sake of his stomach, but if someone betrays you, he will be the first to fight against you.
Do not forget your friend when things go well for you, and do not abandon him because you have acquired wealth.
Every adviser gives advice, but some give advice that benefits themselves.
Guard your heart against the person who advises you. First find out what he has in mind and what he wants from you, because he advises you for his own sake.
He tells you, “You have done well,” and brings you something that will destroy your possessions; then, when you are in trouble, he watches you and laughs at you.
Do not consult someone who is watching for an opportunity against you, and hide your words from someone who envies you.

Do not speak with a woman about someone she is jealous of, and do not consult a coward about war. Do not consult a seller about profit, and do not consult a merchant about business. Do not consult a hardhearted person about giving alms, and do not consult an unjust person about paying wages. Do not consult a lazy person about work, and do not consult a [?] about courage. Do not consult a fool about skill. (Put your dwelling in order, and do not leave it in ruins.) Do not consult any of these about such matters.
Always discuss your plans with a righteous man whom you know to be faithful and to fear the Lord, whose heart is like your own, and who, if you are distressed, will share your suffering.
Stand by the counsel of your own soul, because it is more trustworthy to you than anything else.
For a person's own soul warns him about what will happen to him better than seven [?] watchmen.
Along with all this, pray to the Most High to make your path straight in purity (in righteousness).
Before every deliberation comes a word, and before every deed, counsel.
The course of a man's heart reveals four things:
Whether sorrow or joy, whether death or life—the tongue brings about them all.
There is a person who is learned in everything and knows much, yet cannot benefit himself.
There is someone who is wise in speech but makes himself hated, and every profit passes such a person by.
For God has not granted him favor, and he has departed from all wisdom.
There is someone who is wise for himself and sincere in his speech.
A wise man instructs his people and teaches wisdom to his own people.
A wise man is satisfied with his blessing, and all who see him call him blessed.
A mortal's days are numbered, but the days of Israel cannot be counted.
The person who is wise among his people will receive his reward, and his name will remain forever.
My son, while you are alive, put your soul to the test. Learn what harms it, and do not give it that.
For not everything is suitable for it, and not every soul enjoys everything.
Do not be greedy for every dish, and do not crave every food you see.
For eating too much causes sickness, and gluttony increases vomiting.
Many have been killed by greed, but whoever eats in moderation keeps himself healthy.
Honor the physician, for his honor should match his skill, since God created him too.
Life comes from God, and the physician receives a gift from the king.
Everyone honors the physician for his skill, and he is praised among rulers.
The Lord created medicines from the earth, and a wise man will not despise them.
Was it not through wood that water became sweet, so that his power might be known?
He gave wisdom to human beings so that they might be honored through his glory.
Through it he heals them and soothes all their pain.
From it they prepare medicines with which they heal, and he brings peace to the land.
My son, do not keep silent about your illness. Pray to God, and he will heal you.
Abandon sin, set your hands right, and cleanse [your heart] of all wrongdoing.
Bring your offering, remember the fine flour, and make your sacrifice as rich as you can afford.
Make room for the physician, for God created him too. Do not send him away from you, because you need him too.
For there are times when healing comes through their hands.
They too pray to God to help them and give them relief, and to grant healing through them at all times.
Whoever sins before his Creator will fall into the physician's hands.
My son, weep over the dead, lament him, and grieve. Treat him as his standing deserves, bury him, and do not remain silent about his death (the one who served you).
Weep bitterly and lament deeply. Mourn him as his standing deserves for one day or two days, as the law requires, and then put away your mourning.
Do not let grief enter you, for many have died because of grief, and sorrow of heart breaks one's strength.
Grief and sadness lead to death, and the poor person spends all his days in sadness.
Do not bring grief into your soul; keep sorrow far from you.
Know that there is no remedy: you only hurt yourself and accomplish nothing.
Look at what has happened to me, and know that the same will happen to you too: to me today, and to you tomorrow.
The dead person is at rest. Nevertheless, commemorate him, and then stop weeping so that his soul may rest.
A scribe gains wisdom during his time in office, and the person who does not multiply his work becomes wise.
How can someone become wise when he grips the plow handle, takes pride in his plowing, lashes his oxen, and is occupied with their work, while all his talk is of bulls and oxen?
All his thought is devoted to plowing his furrows, and his care is to feed grain to his oxen (and he works until he tames his calves).

So it is with every craftsman and master craftsman whose night becomes day, and with those who carve and engrave the face of a seal. All his thought is devoted to reproducing each image, and all his planning is devoted to making the seal's engraving precise. His wakefulness is devoted to finishing his work.

So it is also with the smith who sits beside the furnace and practices the craft of ironworking. The furnace smoke irritates his flesh, and the blaze of the fire scorches him. The sound of the hammer deafens his ears, while his eyes examine every detail of the utensil. He thinks about how to finish his work, and his wakefulness is devoted to making his utensils and his metalwork beautiful.
So too with the potter who sits at his work and turns his wheel with his feet. He is always thinking about how to finish his work, and he counts everything he has made.
He shapes clay with his hands and exhausts his strength as he works with his feet. His mind is set on finishing his work, and his care is to [?] his kiln.
All these people rely on the work of their hands, and all are skilled in their work.
Without them a city cannot be inhabited. [?]

They are not consulted in the council, nor seated in the assembly with a ruler. They are not assigned to pronounce judicial sentences, nor appointed as judges or rulers, and they are not found among those who speak in parables.
Instead, they maintain the order of the land, and their prayer is that they may be skilled in their craft.
But skill belongs to the one who has devoted his heart and reflects on the law of the Most High. Wisdom is sought among all the ancients, and she teaches prophecy to people
who have made a name for themselves through faith, and she enters into the parables of the prophets.
She searches out hidden parables and occupies herself with interpreting parables.
She serves among rulers and appears among angels, and she enters the land of foreign nations, for he has tested human beings in both good and evil.
He turns his heart to go to God his Creator and to pray before the Most High. He opens his mouth, makes requests, and pleads concerning his sins.
If God, who is great, wills it and fills him with the spirit of wisdom, he will pour out words of his own wisdom and praise God in prayer.
He will guide his counsel and wisdom and cause him to reflect so that he understands hidden things.
He will reveal the wisdom of his teaching and boast in the law of God's covenant.
Many will praise him for his wisdom, and he will never be blotted out. His memory will not perish, and his name will endure from generation to generation.
Nations will speak of his wisdom, and they will praise him in the assembly.
The endurance of his name is worth more than a thousand, and even after his death his work endures.
I will reflect further and speak. [?]
Listen to me, children of the righteous. Sprout and blossom as a flower blossoms in the dew of the wilderness.
Let your fragrance be as sweet as the fragrance of frankincense. Bring forth your fruit like a rose blossom, and make your fragrance sweet. Sing his praise and bless God for all his works.
Magnify his name and praise him for his glory with a thousand songs and with the harp. Say this when you praise him.
God's work is great and exceedingly good, and everything he ordains has its proper time.
There is no reason to say, “Why is this? Why is that?” Everything will be attended to in its time. By his word he made the water stand like a heap. [?]
The deeds of every living being are before him, and nothing can hide from the sight of his eyes.
From before the world was created and forever, he has known everything, and nothing is strange to him.
No one can say, “Why is this? Why is that?” For everything was created for its own purpose.
His blessing swelled like the water of a river and watered the earth like floodwater.
Likewise, his wrath divided the nations.
His paths are straight for the righteous, but for the sinner they are a stumbling block. He is the one who turned water into salt.
Good was created for the good from the beginning, and likewise evil for sinners.
The chief necessities for human beings are water, fire, iron, salt, wheat grain, honey, milk, the blood of grapes, oil, and clothing.
All these are a blessing to the righteous, but for sinners they turn into harm.
There are spirits created for vengeance. In their anger they intensify their scourge; at their appointed time they unleash their strength and bring their Creator’s scourge upon them.
Fire, hail, famine, and pestilence—all these were created for vengeance.
The teeth of wild animals, scorpions, snakes, and the sword were created to destroy sinners.
But he gives joy through his mercy and provides the world with what it needs. Everything comes to an end when its allotted span is complete and its time has come.
Therefore everything was put in order from its creation. I considered this and set it down in a book.
For all the Lord’s works are good, and he gives human beings everything they need at its proper time.
No one can say, “You created this badly, but you made that well,” for its own day praises each thing.
And now praise the Lord with all your heart and with your mouth, and bless his name at all times.
Great hardship was created for humankind, and a heavy burden rests upon the children of Adam, from the time they come out of their mother’s womb until the day they are buried in the mother of all.
There is terror and fear of heart; anxiety about the day of death rests upon all humankind.
From the one who sits on a royal throne to the poor person who lies on earth and dust.
Anger, jealousy, distress, turmoil, fear of death, rage, and strife: when someone lies down in bed, his thoughts disturb his sleep at night.
His rest is little, almost nothing. In his sleep he is troubled and finds it like [?], and it tosses about the thoughts of his heart, like someone fighting in battle.
When he wakes, he escapes; that very day he marvels at his fear.
This happens to every living human being, and even to animals; but for sinners all this is seven times worse.
Killing, bloodshed, devastation, war, famine, anguish of heart, and scourges.
All these things were created against sinners, and because of them the waters of the flood came.
Everything comes from the earth, and everything returns to the earth; the water of all rivers returns to the sea.
All schemes and injustice will be wiped out, but faithfulness will endure forever.
Unjust wealth dries up like a stream and crashes like loud thunder when it rains.
But when he opens his hands, he gives joy; those who rebel against him will come to an end and perish.
The children of sinners will not put out many branches, and the roots of the unclean are like those on a bare rock.
It makes a sound over all the water and along the bank of a stream, and it stands uprooted before any grass.
But his gracious generosity is like a garden blessed by the Lord, and charity endures forever.
The life of someone who has what he needs and of someone who works is pleasant, but finding a treasure is better than both.
Children and the building of a city make a name great, but better than both is a wife with a good heart.
Wine and music gladden the heart, but better than both is love of wisdom.
The lyre and song delight the soul, but better than both is a pleasant tongue.
Beauty and loveliness please the eye, but better than both is the green growth of crops.
A friend and a protector are useful in their time, but better than both is a good, sensible wife.
Brothers and helpers are for a day of distress, but almsgiving is better than both at bringing deliverance.
Gold and silver make a city strong, but better than both is good advice.
Wealth and possessions gladden the heart, but better than both is the fear of the Lord. The fear of the Lord lacks nothing and needs no help.
The fear of the Lord is like the garden of the Lord in its blessing, and all glory and joy are within it.
My son, do not love begging during your lifetime. It is better to die than to beg.
A man who waits and longs for someone else's table lives as though he were not alive, loving someone else's food. But a wise, disciplined man guards himself against this.
Begging is sweet in the mouth of a shameless person, but a fire burns in his belly.
O death, how bitter is the thought of you when you come upon someone who lives securely, prospers in everything, has strength, and is free to enjoy his food!
O death, your sentence is good when you come upon a poor man who has no strength, upon one who has grown old and [?], who can do nothing and has no one to trust.
Do not fear death's sentence. Remember those who were before you and those who will come after you.
For this is the Lord's sentence upon every living being. Why, then, do you oppose the Lord's will? Even if you live a thousand years, you have no dispute with death about your life.
The children of sinners will be cursed children, and the houses of the wicked will be torn apart.
The children of sinners lose their inheritance, and their disgrace grows along with their offspring.
The children of a sinful father curse him, because they are disgraced on his account.
Woe to you, sinful people, who have abandoned the law of the Most High!
Even if you have children, you will bear them for a curse. [?]
Everything was created from the earth, and its return is to the earth. Likewise, sinners go from a curse into death.
There is mourning for a person's body, but the names of sinners will be erased.
Take care to make a name for yourself; it will outlast ten thousand great treasuries of gold.
It is good to live joyfully through the numbered days of your life, but a good name is better, for it will remain yours forever.
Wisdom shelters her children in peace. But hidden wisdom and a treasure that is not seen—what benefit is there in either?
Someone who conceals his foolishness is better than someone who hides his wisdom.
Therefore respect my words (and my wisdom). Everyone who feels shame guards what is good, and not everyone who is trustworthy is tested in everything.
Shame before father and mother on account of children’s sexual immorality; shame before a ruler and the great for lying.
Be ashamed of changing your word before a ruler or prince; of error before the people and the assembly; and of acting unjustly toward your friend and your companion.

A guest should be ashamed of stealing from his lodging. [?] Be ashamed of approaching to eat someone else's food; of stealing from the possessions of those in your care and from your companion's work.
Be ashamed of turning a deaf ear to someone who visits you; be ashamed of gazing at another man's wife.

Be ashamed of turning a blind eye to your companion in his distress; be ashamed of coveting another person's possessions; be ashamed of speaking with another man's wife, and do not commit adultery with her.

Do not sin with her daughter, and do not approach her bed. Be ashamed of reproaching your friend after giving him something; be ashamed of spreading something you have heard; be ashamed of revealing your friend’s confidential counsel.
If you guard against these things, you will truly be modest and will find favor with everyone.
But do not be ashamed of the following things, and do not show favoritism toward anyone, lest you incur guilt:
Of the law of the Most High and your sacred obligations; and of justice, so that you do not acquit the guilty;
Of settling accounts with your partner concerning your work, concerning sales, and concerning your inheritance;
Concerning balances and measures, and concerning your possessions, whether few or many.
Of everything that profits and benefits you; of disciplining your children; and of flogging the sides of a wicked servant.
A seal is good for a wicked wife, and where many people come in, put things under lock.
Do everything you do by number, measure, and weight. Keep a written record of everything you bring in and take out, give and receive.
And concerning correcting a fool and someone without understanding, and an old man who pursues sexual immorality in his old age. Then you will truly be wise and knowledgeable in the eyes of everyone.
A daughter is a hidden cause of sleeplessness for her father, and worry about her robs him of sleep, from her youth until she grows old without being desired.

Keep a strict watch over a shameless daughter, so that she does not make you a laughingstock to your enemies and a subject of talk among your acquaintances and the assembly of your people, and so that you are not put to shame before the multitude.
Do not admire anyone for their beauty, and do not go among women.
Moths come out of clothing, and every evil comes from women.
A man's wickedness is better than a woman's kindness, and a woman who arouses jealousy is a disgrace.
I will remember the works of the Lord and tell what I have seen, for all the Lord's works came about through his word.
The sun shines and gives light over everything, and the glory of the Lord fills all his works.
Has God not enabled his holy ones to proclaim all his glory, which God, who rules everything, has established? Everything stands firm in his glory.
He traces the depths and the heart and knows their counsels. The Lord knows every thought of the heart and sees the signs of the world.
He declares what has passed and what is to come, and reveals the traces of what is hidden.
No counsel escapes him, and nothing is hidden from him, not even a single word.
He has adorned the greatness of his wisdom, which existed before the world was created and will remain forever. It neither increases nor diminishes, and he has not desired even one counselor.
All his works are beautiful and desirable, and their appearance is like light.
All these things live and remain forever, and they obey him in everything he desires.
Everything is in pairs, one opposite another, and he has made nothing deficient.
He established them, one alongside another, for good. Who can have enough of seeing his goodness?
Above the firmament of heaven in its purity, and the appearance of heaven in his glory.
He makes the sun rise to display its light, and wonderful is its appointed course among the works of heaven.
At noon it dries out the land, and who can withstand its heat?
It makes its heat like a burning furnace, and with threefold heat the sun heats the mountains. A fiery flame blows from it, and the brightness of its light harms the eyes.
Great is the Lord who made it, and at his word it hastens on its journey.
The moon too marks the appointed time for everyone and is a sign for the earth; by it the days are distinguished.
From the moon the sign of festivals is known, a light that comes to an end as it diminishes.
The moon is as its name declares. Wonderful is the way it grows, and marvelous how it [?] within the ordered spectacle of heaven, shining among the host of heaven.
The adornment of heaven is the glory of the stars, and they shine upon the earth in the Lord’s heaven.
At his holy word they travel, each in its appointed order; they neither stray nor depart from their stations.
Look at his rainbow and bless its maker, for its appearance is exceedingly beautiful.
It arches across heaven, and its glory encircles it; the hands of the Most High have bent it.
At his command hail rains down, and lightning hastens at his will.
For this purpose he opens his storehouses, and the clouds fly like birds.
By his greatness he makes the clouds strong, and hailstones break loose.
At his glance the mountains shake, and at his will the east wind blows.
The sound of his thunder frightens the earth, and the tempest of his west wind bends the wind. He scatters snow like flying birds, and it descends like a swarm of locusts.
The beauty of its whiteness is astonishing to the eye, and its showers are marvelous to the mind.
For he mixes his snow and his frost like salt upon the earth. Once its ice has frozen, it breaks into thin shards like crystal.
The east wind blows a cold blast and spreads ice over the water. It settles over every pool of water, resting upon the water like a coat of iron and covering it.
It consumes the mountains, scorches the wilderness, and burns the grass like fire.
A swiftly arriving mist heals everything, and when rain falls upon [?], it brings joy.
By his counsel the deep dries up, and afterward he spreads [?].
Those who travel the sea tell of its hardships, and we marvel when we hear.
There his glory is marvelous and wonderful, and he has made it his own, along with creatures of every kind.
From within it a pleasing fragrance is made for him, and by his word everything comes to be.
We may say much, but we cannot finish; the conclusion of all speech is this: he alone.
How much can we praise him? For he is greater than all his works.
The Lord is awe-inspiring and exceedingly wonderful, and wonderful is his power.
Praise the Lord and exalt him as much as you can, for you will never finish; he is still greater than all this. Exalt him with all your strength, and do not grow weary, for you cannot reach him.
Who has seen him and can tell us about him? And who can exalt him as his greatness deserves?
Much that is unseen is greater than this; we have seen only a little of his work.
For the Lord is the maker of everything, and he gave wisdom to the righteous.
Let us praise honored men, our fathers in their times.
For the Lord gave them abundant glory, and also his greatness, from the creation of the world.
He established them as rulers in their kingdoms—men who made a name for themselves through their strength, counselors through their wisdom, and men who spoke through their prophecies.
Kings of nations in their battles, and their scribes serving the people through their wisdom, through the wisdom of the words in their hearts.
And those who sought out melodies for the harp and singing, and composed as in a book.
And wealthy men whose resources were sufficient for them, who lived securely in their houses.
All these were honored in their times and were held worthy during their lives.
Some among them left a glorious name by which they are spoken of.
There are some whom no one remembers, who perished and became as though they had never been created, as though they had never been born; their children likewise shared their fate.
But these were merciful men whose righteousness was not forgotten.
Their good inheritance will remain with their children forever, resting upon their descendants.
Their children continue to live according to their ordinances. [?]
Their bodies were buried in peace, and their names will endure forever.
The nations will speak of their wisdom, and in the assembly of the nations they will praise them.
Enoch pleased the Lord, and he hid him away. He became an example to the world, so that people might repent.
Noah was found perfectly righteous, and in the days of destruction he became a source of mercy for the world. He remained as a survivor for the earth when the flood came.
He made an everlasting covenant with him, so that the waters of the flood would not destroy every living being.
Abraham is the great father of all the nations, and no one was found as honorable as he.
He kept the law of the Most High and walked with him; (in his flesh) he carried out his law. And when he tested him, he was found faithful.

For this reason he established a covenant with him by an oath, so that the nations would be blessed through his offspring, and so that he would multiply them like the sand of the earth, and his offspring would become numerous like the stars, and he would give them an inheritance from sea to sea and from the rivers to the ends of the earth.
For Isaac also he established the same, because of Abraham his father: a blessing for all humanity, and an ordinance.

It rested upon Jacob, upon his head, and appeared to him in his blessing. He gave it to them as an inheritance, allotted to them their respective inheritances, and divided them among the twelve tribes.
From them he brought forth righteous men who were honored and found favor with all humanity, and were loved by God and by people.
And Moses, whose memory is blessed.
His memory and his likeness were the glory of the holy ones. He made him great, and he became a terror to the enemy.
He performed wonders through his word, praised him before kings, gave him commands concerning his people, and showed him his glory.
He made him holy because of his faithfulness and gentleness, and chose him out of all humanity.

He made him hear his voice and brought him into the thick cloud. He gave him commandments in his presence and taught him the law of life, so that he might teach Jacob his covenant and Israel his judgments.
Aaron too was great like him, a holy man and his brother, from the tribe of Levi.
He established an everlasting ordinance for him and entrusted him with the people's holy offerings. He blessed him with beautiful adornment and clothed him in a robe of glory.
He clothed him and adorned him in every way, and strengthened him in days of might, with his tunics, his full-length robe, and his mantle.
Around him were flowers and many golden bells. Wherever he walked, his steps rang out with a ringing sound, making his sound heard in his sanctuary as a reminder for his people and their children.
There were sacred garments of gold and blue, garments made with scarlet thread, and the breastpiece of judgment, for matters of justice and uprightness.

Garment upon garment, with twisted thread, the distinctive work of a craftsman; and precious stones of astonishing value, chosen and engraved like a seal, with settings of gold and workmanship in precious stones. A memorial was inscribed on it, arranged according to the number of the children of Israel, tribe by tribe.
There was a gold plate above the turban, engraved like a seal with his holiness: the pride of his glory and the work of his might. His adornment was a delight to the eyes and exceedingly beautiful.
Nothing like it had ever been made before him. No one wore anything like it except his children alone and his relatives, forever.
So that they might offer sacrifices to him continually, every morning, day after day.

Moses ordained them and anointed him with holy anointing oil. This became an everlasting ordinance for him and his descendants, for as long as the heavens endure, that they should serve him and be his priests, and bless his people in his name.
He chose him from all the living to bring offerings to the Lord, incense and a memorial of pleasing fragrance, to make atonement for his people.
He gave him his commandments and appointed him to administer his justice and judgments, to teach Jacob his testimony and instruct Israel in his law.
Strangers opposed him and were jealous of him in the wilderness: the men of Dathan and Abiram and the rebellious company of Korah. They died by plague and destruction.
The Lord saw them, and they did not please him. He destroyed them in his wrath, did an astonishing thing against them, and consumed them in a blazing fire.
He increased Aaron's glory and gave him his portion, the first of their grain, and set before them grain to satisfy them.
So that they might eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to him and to his descendants.
He was not to share in the people's land or inherit an inheritance with the people, for he is your portion and your inheritance.
Phinehas son of Eleazar was third in glory, because he was zealous for the fear of the Lord. He stood up to rebuke the people, and in the generosity of his soul he came forward willingly for Israel.

Because of this, he established a covenant of peace with him, so that he might teach his people the ordinances of the holy ones, and so that the high priesthood might belong to him and his descendants forever.

The inheritance of David, who was from the tribe of Judah, passed to his son, and the allotted kingship belonged to his descendants according to his law; his inheritance likewise belonged to him and his descendants.
May he give them wisdom in their hearts to judge his people righteously, so that they do not squander their blessings and their glory throughout all their days.

Joshua son of Nun was mighty in battle and succeeded Moses in prophecy. In keeping with his name, he became great and saved his chosen ones. He took vengeance on their enemies so that he might give Israel their land as an inheritance.
He was praised when he raised his hands and lowered his spear against their cities.
Who before him had been like him? The Lord himself fought their enemies for them.
Was it not through his hand that the sun stood still and one day became as long as two days?
He called upon the Most High and Mighty One when his enemies pressed him on every side. The great Lord answered him with hailstones and mighty power.

He rained them down upon the nation that fought against them. On the slope he destroyed those who battled against them, so that the nations might know his power, for it is the Lord who fights against them. He made his power accompany them.
In the days of Moses, he and Caleb son of Jephunneh acted mercifully toward them. They stood against the enemy, kept the people from sin, and made them stop their wicked grumbling.
But these two alone survived out of six hundred thousand foot soldiers and entered the land flowing with milk and honey.
God gave Caleb strength and remained with him until his old age. He brought him up into the highlands, and his children shared their inheritance.
This was so that all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.
And all their rulers, each by name, and all whose hearts did not stray, and all who did not abandon the Lord—may their memory be blessed.
May their bones rejoice where they lie, and may their children be blessed and honored.
Samuel was beloved by the Lord and was a prophet of the Lord. He appointed a king and anointed a king for his people.
He judged the assembly according to the Lord's law, and the Lord showed mercy to Jacob.
Through his faithfulness his prophecy as a prophet was confirmed, and through his words he proved to be a trustworthy seer.
He called on the mighty Lord when his enemies distressed him and hemmed him in, offering a suckling lamb as a sacrifice.
The Lord thundered in heaven and made his voice heard with a mighty crash.
He crushed the kings of Tyre and all the kings of the Philistines.

Before the day of his death arrived, he declared before the Lord and his anointed that he had taken nothing from any of them, from their possessions down to their sandals. Not one of them accused him.
He prophesied after his death and told the king of his death. He raised his voice from within the earth, and through his prophecy he blotted out the people's transgression.
After him Nathan arose and prophesied in the days of David.
Just as the fat is separated from the sacrifice of well-being, so David was set apart from the children of Israel.
Lions were like young goats to him, and bears were like lambs.
Did he not kill a giant in his youth and remove his people's disgrace, when he raised his hand and struck him with a stone, piercing Goliath's forehead and striking his skull?
For he called on the Lord Most High, who gave strength to his right hand to kill a mighty warrior in battle and to raise the horn of his people.
He rewarded him with acclaim for ten thousand, with song and music in the Lord's blessing, and he was crowned with a crown of glory.
He crushed his enemies all around, humiliated the hostile Philistines, and broke their horns, which remain broken to this day.
In everything he did, he trusted in him. With words of praise to the Most High and Holy One, he praised him in all his deeds, gave thanks to his Creator, and loved him.
He appointed singers before the altar, and the sound of their voices was melodious and sweet.
He made the festivals beautiful and brought joy throughout the year. He praised his holy name, and from dawn his holiness was proclaimed.
The Lord blotted out his sins and raised his horn forever. He gave him a blessed kingdom and a throne of glory for Israel.
After him his wise son succeeded him and, because of him, lived in ease.
Solomon reigned in days of peace, and the Lord gave him rest on every side. He established a house in his name and built a sanctuary in his name forever.
Your wisdom increased from your youth, and your wisdom was full like the waters of the Tekeze.
Your understanding covered the earth, and you multiplied your proverbs and the interpretations of your sayings.
Your name was heard as far away as the distant islands, and they loved you because of your peace.
For your songs, your proverbs, and your speech, they marveled at you throughout the regions because of the interpretation of your words.
In the name of the Lord, who is called the God of Israel, you made gold as plentiful as lead and heaped up silver like tin.
Women turned your mind aside, and you were enslaved by your flesh.
You dishonored your glory and defiled your offspring. You brought ruin and punishment upon your children, and your folly terrified me.
Your rule was divided, and a rebellious kingdom arose from Ephraim.

But the Lord did not abandon his mercy, nor will he destroy his work. He did not wipe out the children of the righteous, nor will he eliminate the offspring of those who love him. He gave Jacob a remnant, and David a root descended from him.

Solomon rested with his fathers and left behind him an offspring for the people: Rehoboam, a fool without understanding, who caused the people to rebel through his counsel; and Jeroboam, who led Israel astray and made a path of sin for Ephraim.
Their sins multiplied more and more, and he drove them out of their land.
They pursued every kind of evil until their punishment overtook them.
Then Elijah arose, a prophet like fire, and his word burned like a flame.
He brought famine upon them and reduced their numbers in his zeal.
By the word of the Lord he shut up the heavens and brought fire down from heaven three times.
How glorious you were, Elijah, in your glory! Who could boast as you could?
You raised a corpse from the dead and from the grave by the word of the Most High.
You brought kings down to death, and nobles from their beds.
You who [?] judgment at Sinai, and justice and vengeance at Horeb.
You anoint kings and exact vengeance from them, and prophets took your place.
You ascended in a blazing fire, in chariots and with horses of fire.
You had judgment recorded for your appointed time, to cool wrath before punishment, to turn a father's heart toward his children, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
Blessed are those who know you and those adorned with your love. We too will live (because of you).
Elijah ascended in a blaze of fire, and Elisha was filled with his (holy) spirit. In his days, angels did not frighten him, and no one hindered him.
Nothing was beyond his power, and even after his death his body prophesied.
During his life he performed wonders, and even in his death his works were marvelous.

Despite all this, the people did not repent or abandon their sins until they were taken captive from their country and scattered throughout the earth. Only a few of the people remained, and a messenger from the house of David.
Some among them did what was good, and some multiplied their sins.
Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into its midst. He cut through rock with iron and built a reservoir.
In his days Sennacherib came up and sent Rabshakeh, who went to him. He raised his hand against Zion, grew arrogant, and spoke boastfully.
At that time their hearts trembled, and their hands went limp like those of a woman giving birth.
They called upon the merciful Lord and raised their hands to him. The Holy One quickly heard them from heaven and delivered them through Isaiah.
He killed the Persians, their adversaries, and his angel crushed them.
For Hezekiah did what pleased the Lord and held firmly to the ways of his father David, as the prophet Isaiah commanded. Isaiah was faithful, and his vision was great.
In his days the sun went backward, and he added years to the king’s life.
Through a great spirit he saw the future and comforted those who mourned in Zion.
He declared what would happen forever, and hidden things before they happened.
The memory of Josiah is good, a remembrance of wisdom, like incense whose fragrance has been prepared. It is sweet as honey in every mouth and like music at a drinking feast.
He acted rightly and turned the people back, and he removed every defiling sin.
He directed his heart toward the Lord, and in the days of sinners he upheld righteousness.
But David, Hezekiah, Josiah, and all those sinned and went astray and abandoned the law of the Most High, and the kings of Judah came to an end.
For they handed over their power to a stranger and their glory to another people.
They burned the chosen and holy city and destroyed its streets through Jeremiah.
For they mistreated him, though he had been consecrated from his mother’s womb to be a prophet, to uproot and destroy, and likewise to plant and build.
Ezekiel also saw a vision of his glory, and his vision was above a chariot of cherubim.
He remembered the enemy in wrath, and in goodness he made straight the paths of the righteous.
The bones of the twelve prophets sprouted in their resting places. He comforted Jacob and delivered them through the faithfulness of their hope.
How, then, shall we magnify Zerubbabel? He was like a signet ring on the right hand.
And Joshua son of Jozadak also: they built the house in their days and made it great for the people of the Lord, worthy of everlasting glory.
Great is the remembrance of Nehemiah, who raised our fallen walls for us, set up gates, made bars, and built our houses for us.
No one was created on earth like Enoch, and they took him away from the earth.
No man was born like Joseph. He became a messenger to his brothers and a source of strength to his people, and his bones received favor.
Shem and Seth were honored above other human beings, and Adam above every living thing that was created.
Simon, son of [?], the high priest, built the temple during his lifetime and strengthened the temple building in his days.
Likewise, he built what would double its height and made a fine garment for a priest to wrap himself in.
In his days he built water fountains and reservoirs whose water was as abundant as the sea.
He cared for his people against ruin, sought the foundation of the city, and killed [?].
And he was glorified when the people returned and when the doorway of the house was opened.
Like the morning star among the clouds, and like the full moon on feast days.
And like the sun shining in the sanctuary of the Most High, and like the radiant splendor of the rainbow.
And like a rose blossom in the month of [?], and like a plant bearing fruit beside a flowing stream, and like a shoot of frankincense in the days of harvest.
And like incense in the fire upon a censer, and like a vessel of beaten gold.
And like an olive tree whose fruit has sprouted, and like a precious pearl in an ornament, and like a tall cypress tree beneath the clouds.
Such was he when he put on his glorious robe, when he put on the adornment in which he took pride, and when he went up the steps of the altar and was glorified in the robe of holy splendor.
When he received the sacrificial meat from the priests’ hands, standing at his place of service, his brothers stood around him, encircling and surrounding him like palm shoots.
And all the descendants of Aaron were in their ranks, with the offering of the Lord in their hands, before the whole assembly of Israel.
And they performed their service at the altar and made the offering pleasing to the Most High, who rules over all.
And he raised his hand with the bowl and poured out the blood of the grape. He poured it at the base of the altar, a pleasing fragrance to the Most High, the King of all kings.
And the descendants of Aaron cried out and blew the hammered-metal horn, making its sound heard loudly as a remembrance before the Most High.
At that moment all the people together fell down and bowed with their faces to the ground, praising the Lord their God, the Most High, who rules over all.
And the singers praised him with their voices, and the mighty roar of their voices filled the whole house.
And the people prayed to the Lord Most High and made their requests before the Merciful One, until they completed what the law of the Lord required and finished their service.
Then he came down and raised his hands over the whole assembly of the children of Israel, to give them the Lord’s blessing with his lips, and so that they might glory in his name.
And they bowed down again so that the Most High might reveal his blessing.
And now bless the God of all, who does great things everywhere, who prolongs our days from our mother's womb and deals with us according to his mercy.
And he gave us joy of heart. May he establish peace in our days and over Israel for all the days of eternity.
And his mercy proved faithful toward us, and he redeemed us in our days.
My soul hates two nations, and the third is not a people.
Those who live on Mount Samaria, and Philistia, and the people of the Amorites who live in Shechem.
I, Jesus son of Sirach, son of Eleazar, of Jerusalem, who poured forth wisdom from his heart, wrote instruction in wisdom and discipline in this book.
Blessed is the one who acts in this way, who becomes wise and observes this.
Whoever does this will be capable of everything, for the light of the Lord is his path.
I praise you, Lord and King, and I glorify you, my God and my Savior, and I trust in your name.

For you became my helper and my shelter, and you redeemed my body from death, from the snare of a slanderous tongue, and from the thousands who practice falsehood. In the presence of all who rose against me, you became my helper and my shelter.

And you redeemed me according to the abundance of your mercy and for the sake of your name. Like those who gnash their teeth, ready to devour, so they sought my life amid the great suffering that befell me.
And like one surrounded by fire who is not scorched in the midst of the fire.
And from the depths below, from the belly of death, from a slanderous tongue, and from a lying word.
An unjust tongue that slanders before the king brought (my life and) my soul to death, and my life drew near the grave.
They hemmed me in on every side, and I had no helper. I looked around to see whether anyone would take notice of me, but there was no one.
I remembered your mercy, Lord, and your deeds since the creation of the world, for blessed are those who hope in you, and you save them from the hands of their enemies.
You raised me from the earth, from my sin, and I asked to be saved from death.
I said to God, “My Father and my Lord, do not abandon me in my distress, in the days of the arrogant, when there is no help.”
I will praise your name continually; I will glorify you and speak. And he heard my prayer.
He saved me from death and rescued me from an evil day. For this reason I will glorify you and praise you and bless your name, Lord.
While I was young, before I went astray, I sought wisdom and put her first in my prayer.
Before the sanctuary I prayed for her; I continually sought her.
Her fruit sprouted like the [?] of wheat, and my heart rejoiced in her. My foot stood in righteousness, and from my youth I followed her footsteps.
I listened a little with my ear and chose her, and I gained much wisdom for myself.
Through her I was exalted, and I will praise the one who gave me wisdom.
I resolved to practice her and was zealous for what is good, and he will not be put to shame.
My soul grew strong through her, and I acted wisely in my deeds. I raised my hands high and lamented my ignorance of her.
I directed my soul toward her and found her in purity. From the beginning I set my heart on her, and for this reason he did not abandon me.
My inward parts were stirred for her and sought her. For this reason I acquired a good possession.
God gave me my reward through my tongue, and I will praise him for it.
Come near to me, you foolish people, and stay in the house of wisdom.
How have you missed her? Speak about this. Your souls have grown exceedingly thirsty.
I opened my mouth and said, “Acquire her for yourselves without payment.”
Bow your necks and carry her burden, and let your souls receive wisdom. She is close at hand to be found.
Look and see with your own eyes how little I labored and how much rest I found for myself.
Prefer wisdom to vast amounts of gold beyond counting; acquire her for yourselves.
Let your souls rejoice in his mercy, and do not be ashamed to praise him.
Do your work before its appointed time comes, so that he may give you your reward in his time.
